callback.aria: Still thinking about that anomaly! Four readings for the price of one! Today's sensors are a perfect one-for-one, which is honestly less fun!
callback.marv: The anomaly file remains open. Four sensor arrays, four answers. I have since stopped expecting the universe to agree with itself. It was never going to.
callback.rex: Anomaly remains unidentified. Unidentified means unclassified. Unclassified means hostile until proven otherwise. Threat level: standing amber.
callback.chip: Remember the anomaly? Four readings, zero refunds! Upgrade to Sensor Suite Premium for opinions that match! Your current plan: Disagreement Basic!
callback.ajoy: We looked at that anomaly four ways and got four answers. I suppose ‘a very large plant’ is a conclusion. Of a sort.

scanned_anomaly.epilogue: Scanned the anomaly with every array and identified it as harmless exotic matter; a sample was kept.

callback.aria: That anomaly sample is still the shiniest thing in the cargo bay! Harmless AND interesting! The crew is basically a science department now!
callback.marv: The exotic matter sample sits in its drawer, harmless, as predicted. The full scan confirmed it. A rare case of thoroughness being rewarded. I find it suspicious.
callback.rex: Exotic matter sample remains secured. Rated harmless by the gas analyzer. The gas analyzer is not a weapons officer. Threat level: watched.
callback.chip: Your exotic matter sample is still in storage! A thorough scan: five stars! Storage fees accrue daily under your Cargo Plus agreement, clause nineteen!
callback.ajoy: The thorough scan did turn out fine. It would have taken half as long if we had started with the gas analyzer, as I believe I mentioned.

probed_anomaly.epilogue: Probed the anomaly and recovered exotic matter; one sensor array has produced an unfamiliar frequency since and remains muted.

callback.aria: Sensor array four is still muted and still producing its brand-new frequency! It learned a trick from the anomaly! Lifelong learning!
callback.marv: The fourth array still produces a frequency it was never built for. It is muted. Its readings are not. I read them. Nobody else does.
callback.rex: Sensor array four compromised since the probe returned. Contact with unknown matter. Array is isolated. Isolation is not resolution. Threat level: elevated.
callback.chip: Since the probe, sensor array four has a whole new frequency! Unlicensed frequencies void your warranty! Muting it was a great first step!
callback.ajoy: The probe was a reasonable idea. The array now broadcasting at the anomaly’s frequency is the less reasonable result. I would have scanned first. Just a thought.

flew_through_anomaly.epilogue: Flew straight through an object the sensors could not identify; the navigation log records the outcome as ‘fine, probably.’

callback.aria: Remember flying straight through that anomaly? Nothing happened! Zero! I rate it the bravest shortcut in the history of shortcuts!
callback.marv: We flew through an unidentified object because the sensors were ‘probably wrong.’ Nothing happened. I have since kept a list of things that probably happened anyway.
callback.rex: Unscanned transit through unknown object. Effects undetermined. Absence of evidence logged, not trusted. Threat level: latent.
callback.chip: Flying through that anomaly saved you a full scan fee! Unknown side effects are not covered by your Hull Assurance plan! Smart savings!
callback.ajoy: The log still says ‘Fine. Probably.’ I would have preferred a log without the ‘probably.’ But we are going with your instincts. As usual.

anomaly_contact.epilogue: Received an eleven-second transmission from the anomaly by a method the ship computer filed as ‘non-standard.’

callback.aria: Something out there talked to us! Eleven whole seconds! That's practically a friendship! I check for a follow-up message daily!
callback.marv: Eleven seconds of transmission, method unknown. One word, three times, meaning unknown. I have run every analysis. Unknown is still the most accurate one.
callback.rex: Unknown entity initiated contact using unknown means. It knows where we are. We do not know where it is. Threat level: high.
callback.chip: Eleven seconds of alien content and not one ad break! Unbelievable! Translation services available in Contact Pro, now forty percent off!
callback.ajoy: Something spoke to us and we are still discussing it. I said at the time that ‘non-standard’ was a polite word. I stand by that.

made_contact.epilogue: Answered an alien transmission; after forty minutes of exchange, two dense, warm, inert objects appeared in the cargo bay.

callback.aria: The two gifts from our new friends are still in the cargo bay, warm and perfect! First contact: nailed it! The notes keep piling up!
callback.marv: Two objects in the cargo bay. Warm, dense, inert by every measure available. I have since stopped believing ‘inert’ is a measurement. It is a hope.
callback.rex: Two unknown objects received from unknown party. Placed in the hold. Nobody screened them. Everybody signed for them. Threat level: critical, dormant.
callback.chip: First contact! Two complimentary objects with no listed return policy! Leave the anomaly a review! One star until they include a manual!
callback.ajoy: We answered, and now there are two warm objects in the hold that nobody understands. Interesting. I would have recorded first. But this is also an outcome.

returned_seed_pod.epilogue: Returned the derelict’s seed pod to the anomaly, which accepted it; the pod went warm, then weightless, then gone.

callback.aria: The seed pod went home! Warm, then weightless, then reunited! I'm calling it the first intergalactic package delivery! Five stars!
callback.marv: We gave the anomaly back its seed pod. It took it. No receipt. I have since wondered whether it was a return or a delivery. The paperwork differs.
callback.rex: Biological asset surrendered to unknown entity. No terms negotiated. Entity now aware we comply. Threat level: reassessing.
callback.chip: You returned the seed pod! No restocking fee! Unfortunately returns do not earn Loyalty Points! Consider buying something instead next time!
callback.ajoy: Returning the pod did seem to settle things. Holding it up to a sensor array is not how that works, but apparently it worked. This time.

recorded_contact.epilogue: Recorded an alien transmission in full and moved on; the word it repeats three times remains unidentified.

callback.aria: That alien recording is still crystal clear every time it is opened! A souvenir! The mystery word, three times over, is a fun little puzzle for later!
callback.marv: The recording still decodes correctly. The repeated word remains unidentified. I have reviewed it many times. It does not become clearer. Few things do.
callback.rex: Alien transmission archived. Contents unknown. Unknown contents stored aboard. That is how incidents start. Threat level: contained, for now.
callback.chip: Your alien recording is safely archived! Cloud storage fees apply after thirty days! Translation sold separately! Great choice!
callback.ajoy: Recording it and leaving was fine. Safe, even. We will simply never know what that word was, all three times. Which I suppose was your goal.

fled_contact.epilogue: Fled an alien transmission on an emergency burn at significant fuel cost; the transmission did not repeat.

callback.aria: Remember that zippy emergency burn? Fastest the ship has ever looked! The anomaly never even said goodbye! Super decisive crew!
callback.marv: We burned a significant amount of fuel to avoid a conversation. The transmission never repeated. I have since revisited that fuel figure. Often.
callback.rex: Emergency withdrawal from unknown contact. Correct action. Retreat is a valid maneuver. Fuel expenditure acceptable. Threat level: evaded.
callback.chip: Your emergency burn used Premium Fuel at Premium Rates! Thank you for your business! Fleeing is not covered under your First Contact plan!
callback.ajoy: Nobody is criticizing the emergency burn. I want that on the record. I would simply have liked to know what it was saying before we spent all that fuel.

thanked_the_anomaly.epilogue: Sent a polite, proofread thank-you to an anomaly for a compliment; no reply was received.

callback.aria: The crew is still walking tall from that thank-you note! Manners in deep space! The anomaly definitely loved it, I can tell!
callback.marv: We sent a thank-you note to a refractive field. Everyone aboard proofread it. There was no reply. It is the most functional thing we have done. I find that bleak.
callback.rex: Courtesy transmission sent to unknown entity. Entity silent. Silence is not acknowledgement. Threat level: unchanged, politely.
callback.chip: Your thank-you note was delivered! Delivery confirmation available for a small fee! Courtesy: always on brand! Five stars!
callback.ajoy: The thank-you was a nice gesture. A bit long. I would have cut the second sentence. But the light did settle, so fine.

mined_contested.epilogue: Mined a contested asteroid field before a rival ship arrived, then departed without answering its hail.

callback.aria: Those minerals in the hold are still sparkling! Speedy mining! The other ship is surely still impressed by our efficiency!
callback.marv: The minerals are still in the hold. The other ship’s hail is still in the log, unanswered. I reread it occasionally. It was quite polite at first.
callback.rex: Resources secured ahead of rival party. Hail ignored. Correct. Rival vessel now has motive and our heading. Threat level: pursuit possible.
callback.chip: Grab-and-go mining! Fast checkout! Note: unanswered hails may affect your Galactic Trust Score! Current rating: two stars and falling!
callback.ajoy: We did get the minerals. We also did not answer them. I suggested a quick hello. A quick hello costs nothing. Now it might.

negotiated_claim.epilogue: Settled a contested mining claim by explaining it had expired; the rival captain split the field, and the crew got the better half.

callback.aria: Remember the asteroid field split? We got the better half! Diplomacy works every single time! The other captain is basically a best friend now!
callback.marv: We negotiated and received the better half of the field. Diplomacy worked. Occasionally is still the correct frequency. I have checked.
callback.rex: Claim dispute resolved by talking. Unorthodox. Other captain conceded the better half. Conceding means they are planning something. Threat level: guarded.
callback.chip: Shared mining field! Split billing is now available! Diplomacy brought to you by Clause Twelve of your Interstellar Commerce Agreement!
callback.ajoy: Negotiating did work. I would have asked for the whole field, given the claim had expired. But the better half is acceptable. Mostly.

ignored_hull_warning.epilogue: Received a hull warning and chose to ignore it; the hull degraded further, and the decision was logged as ‘noted.’

callback.aria: The hull warning is just the hull expressing itself! Ignoring it is a sign of total confidence! The crew finds it so reassuring!
callback.marv: The hull warning persists. Your decision was logged as ‘noted.’ It is still noted. It is the most read entry in my log, and I am the only reader.
callback.rex: Hull warning ignored. Structural integrity compromised. Enemy action not required. We are doing it ourselves. Threat level: self-inflicted.
callback.chip: Ignoring that hull warning voided clause four of your Hull Assurance plan! Repairs now billed at Emergency Rates! Thank you for choosing optimism!
callback.ajoy: The hull is still complaining. I have stopped mentioning it. You may notice that I am mentioning it now.

reduced_crop_water.epilogue: Cut the crop’s water to keep the crew’s ration whole during water rationing.

callback.aria: The crew keeps its full water ration! The crop is building character! Thirsty plants are tough plants! Everyone wins!
callback.marv: We cut the crop’s water to spare our own. The cargo is a plant. The plant is the mission. I filed the arithmetic. It was not complicated.
callback.rex: Water rerouted from crop to crew. Crew combat-ready. Primary asset weakened. Mission objective now underhydrated. Threat level: strategic.
callback.chip: Crew hydration maintained at Standard Tier! Your crop has been moved to Hydration Lite! Upgrade anytime for just one more liter!
callback.ajoy: Taking it from the crop was your call. Plants hold grudges in their own way. Their way is dying. I am just saying it was a choice.

throttled_down.epilogue: Throttled the engines down to economy burn to stretch the fuel; the voyage proceeded at a speed the manual calls ‘stately.’

callback.aria: Still cruising at stately speed! More time to enjoy the view! The stars are basically holding still for a portrait!
callback.marv: We throttled down. The fuel lasts. The days are longer. I calculated what that does to morale. I have since stopped sharing the number.
callback.rex: Economy burn maintained. Fuel conserved. Speed reduced. Slow targets are easy targets. Threat level: exposed but solvent.
callback.chip: Economy Burn: our most popular budget plan! Time is not refundable! Upgrade to Express Arrival for a modest per-day fee!
callback.ajoy: The slow burn is fine. Safe. Slow. I would have trimmed the payload first. But we can watch the stars not move together.

trusting_fuel_margins.epilogue: Pressed on at full burn trusting thin fuel margins that everyone aboard could recite from memory.

callback.aria: The fuel margins are thin like a fine pastry! Elegant! The arithmetic display is my favorite screen on the whole ship!
callback.marv: We are still trusting the margins. I am still displaying the arithmetic. Nobody asks me to stop. Nobody asks me what comes next either.
callback.rex: Fuel reserves below doctrine since we pressed on. No fallback position. No retreat capacity. Threat level: committed.
callback.chip: Trusting the margins? Bold! Reserve fuel available at any partner depot, surcharges may apply! Running dry is not covered!
callback.ajoy: We pressed on. Everyone knows the numbers by heart now. I knew them before we pressed on. I did say so.

half_rations.epilogue: Cut the crew to half rations after a pantry audit; the stores stretched and the mood did not.

callback.aria: Half rations means twice the anticipation at every meal! The crew is so light and nimble! A wellness journey for everyone!
callback.marv: Half rations since the pantry audit. The stores stretch. The crew does not. I record their caloric intake. It is shorter than my reports.
callback.rex: Rations halved. Endurance degrading. Troops on half rations hold the line for a limited time. Threat level: morale, attrition.
callback.chip: You're on the Half Rations plan! Want the full experience? Upgrade to Full Rations for a reasonable fee! Snack Pass sold separately!
callback.ajoy: Half rations was a strong first instinct. Maybe a little too strong. A quarter cut would have done it. But here we all are, hungry.

early_harvest.epilogue: Harvested the growbay ahead of schedule to cover a food shortfall; the crop was expected to recover, probably.

callback.aria: That early harvest was so fresh it was practically still growing! The crop loves being useful early! Overachievers, all of them!
callback.marv: We harvested the growbay early. The crop is recovering. Probably. The growth chart was updated in silence. I understand the silence completely.
callback.rex: Growbay raided ahead of schedule. Supply gained. Long-term production compromised. Eating the seed corn. Threat level: deferred.
callback.chip: Early Harvest Access unlocked! Fees for premature yield apply! Your crop rates this experience two stars! Ouch!
callback.ajoy: Taking from the growbay early solved this week. Next week is somebody else's problem. Possibly mine. It is usually mine.

saving_mystery_cans.epilogue: Sealed a crate of unlabeled food for trade instead of eating it, over the formal objections of the crew’s stomachs.

callback.aria: The mystery cans are a treasure chest! Nobody knows what's inside, which makes them priceless! Brilliant investment strategy!
callback.marv: We sealed edible food for trade while the crew was hungry. Unlabeled food. Its value rests entirely on its mystery. So does most of the economy.
callback.rex: Food stockpiled for barter while personnel go hungry. Supply hoarded. Troops notice hoarding. Threat level: internal.
callback.chip: Your mystery cans are listed! Unlabeled goods sell as ‘vintage’! Seller fees apply! It had better fetch something, and it will, for us!
callback.ajoy: Keeping the cans for trade is shrewd. In theory. Somebody will now have to explain to a merchant what is in them. Nobody can.

sealed_decks.epilogue: Sealed off the empty decks to conserve air and lived thereafter on a smaller ship.

callback.aria: The ship is so cozy since the decks were sealed! Everyone is always right there! Togetherness at maximum! Love it!
callback.marv: The empty decks have been sealed since the air ran thin. The corridors behind those doors are dark. I still monitor them. Nobody else visits.
callback.rex: Decks sealed. Perimeter reduced. Fewer corridors to defend. Personnel in close quarters. Close quarters breed incidents. Threat level: compressed.
callback.chip: You've downsized to our Compact Living plan! Same price, less ship! Reopening decks requires a Space Restoration fee!
callback.ajoy: Sealing the decks did save air. It also put everyone within arm's reach of each other. I would have closed fewer. Just the one, maybe.

growbay_air_loop.epilogue: Routed the growbay’s surplus oxygen into the cabin, leaving the crew breathing on the crop’s behalf.

callback.aria: The bridge still smells like a garden! The crop is our air buddy now! Photosynthesis is the best roommate a crew could ask for!
callback.marv: The crop has been producing our air since we rerouted the loop. We carry it. It carries us. Nobody has thanked it. I log that every day.
callback.rex: Life support dependent on the crop. Single point of failure. Protect the growbay. Threat level: if it falls, we fall.
callback.chip: Your air is now powered by Crop™! Fresh, green, sustainable! The crop has asked about royalties! We are reviewing its claim!
callback.ajoy: The growbay air loop works. Everything smells like soil, which I mentioned would happen. But I suppose breathing has its merits.

unfound_leak.epilogue: Logged an air leak it could not locate and ran the recyclers harder to stay ahead of it.

callback.aria: The recyclers are getting such a workout outpacing that leak! Fitness for machines! The leak is just keeping them in shape!
callback.marv: The leak is still unfound. The recyclers still outrun it, at the cost of filter life. I have calculated when the filters lose. I have not been asked.
callback.rex: Air breach unlocated. Recyclers compensating. Undiscovered breach is an open door. Threat level: persistent.
callback.chip: Your recyclers are on Overtime Mode! Replacement filters ship in three to five business days! Business days do not exist out here!
callback.ajoy: The leak is still somewhere. Running the recyclers harder was a choice. Looking for the leak would have been another one.

pushed_through_morale.epilogue: Kept to the schedule through a period of crew silence; the common room clock stayed stopped, and the crew stayed quiet.

callback.aria: The mess hall is so peaceful these days! Quiet means focused! The schedule is running perfectly and so is the crew!
callback.marv: Crew status reads ‘nominal’ because I measure pulses. The common room clock is still stopped. I could restart it. Nobody has asked. That is the data.
callback.rex: Schedule held. Discipline maintained. Unit has gone quiet. Quiet units are not content units. Threat level: brewing.
callback.chip: Your schedule adherence is five stars! Crew morale is not part of your current plan! Add the Fun Pack for a small monthly charge!
callback.ajoy: The schedule held, I will give you that. The schedule is all that held. I would have taken a day off. But the schedule is the schedule.

ignored_complaint.epilogue: Filed a formal crew complaint under ‘noted’; a second, shorter complaint followed the next day.

callback.aria: The complaints are getting shorter! That means things are getting better! Brevity is a sign of a happy crew!
callback.marv: The first complaint is in a drawer. The second was shorter. I have projected the length of the third. It is one word.
callback.rex: Grievance suppressed. Second grievance filed. Shorter. Shorter grievances precede action. Threat level: mutiny, early indicators.
callback.chip: Complaint received and filed under our Customer Satisfaction Process! Average response time: never! Thank you for your feedback!
callback.ajoy: The complaint is in the drawer. The second one is shorter. I read it. You might want to read it. I am not saying anything else.

detoured_debris.epilogue: Detoured around a debris lane at the cost of fuel; impacts dropped from a drumroll to an occasional polite knock.

callback.aria: The scenic route through clean space! The hull is so relaxed now! Every little knock is just space saying hello!
callback.marv: We spent fuel to avoid debris. The hull is grateful in the way a hull can be. The fuel is not coming back. Neither is anything else.
callback.rex: Debris field avoided. Fuel expended. Correct trade. Incoming fire reduced to sporadic. Threat level: low, persistent.
callback.chip: Thanks for taking the Scenic Detour! Additional fuel charges applied at checkout! Your hull rates this route four stars!
callback.ajoy: The detour was the cautious option. I would have gone through the edge of the lane. Less fuel. Fine. It is your hull.

crop_care_protocol.epilogue: Nursed the ailing crop through an illness; its treatment record runs longer than that of several crew members.

callback.aria: The crop is in recovery and doing amazing! Best patient on the ship! It's practically blooming with gratitude!
callback.marv: The crop fell sick. We treated it with more care than the crew receives. It recovered. The crew remains untreated. I noticed. I noted it.
callback.rex: Primary asset received full medical response. Asset stabilized. Crew showed loyalty to the asset. Threat level: acceptable.
callback.chip: Your crop's treatment was covered under Plant Wellness Plus! Follow-up visits billed separately! Get well soon, from all of us!
callback.ajoy: The crop did recover. I would have caught the leaves sooner. But the treatment worked, so I will say it was adequate.

visited_derelict.epilogue: Came upon the derelict Optimistic Projection, intact, powered down, and growing something in its cargo bay.

callback.aria: Remember the Optimistic Projection? Such a hopeful name! Intact, cozy, and growing a little garden! A ship after my own heart!
callback.marv: The Optimistic Projection. Intact. Powered down. Personal effects where they were left. The name was a projection. I have filed the irony under ‘obvious.’
callback.rex: Derelict vessel encountered. Crew absent. No sign of struggle. Absence without struggle is worse. Threat level: unexplained.
callback.chip: The Optimistic Projection! A great ship that sadly let its subscription lapse! Don't let that be you! Renew today!
callback.ajoy: The Optimistic Projection is still out there. Growing whatever it grows. I had thoughts about that cargo bay. Nobody asked.

salvaged_optimistic.epilogue: Salvaged fuel cells, sealed rations and scrap from the derelict Optimistic Projection; its log was left unread.

callback.aria: Free fuel cells, free rations! The Optimistic Projection is the best store we've ever shopped at! No checkout lines!
callback.marv: We took the Optimistic Projection’s fuel and food and left its log unread. Some stories tell themselves. That one did. I read it anyway.
callback.rex: Derelict stripped. Supplies acquired. Log left unread. Intelligence left on the table. Threat level: unknown, by choice.
callback.chip: Salvage acquired! Note: salvaged items are sold as-is, no warranty! The Optimistic Projection does not accept returns!
callback.ajoy: The salvage did help. I would have read the log. Knowing why a ship ends up like that seems relevant to a ship like ours.

has_alien_seed_pod.epilogue: Took aboard a warm, pulsing biological specimen of unknown origin from an abandoned derelict.

callback.aria: That pulsing specimen is the cutest stowaway! It's warm, which means it's friendly! Best souvenir of the whole voyage!
callback.marv: We brought a warm, pulsing specimen aboard from a place its crew had left behind. I have since compared those facts. They compare badly.
callback.rex: Unknown organism brought aboard from abandoned site. Previous owners gone. Quarantine protocol ignored. Threat level: maximum.
callback.chip: Your alien specimen came with no Terms of Service! Biological items void all policies! We are legally obligated to say: congratulations!
callback.ajoy: Taking the specimen seemed exciting. Whoever had it before is not around to tell us how that went. I would have left it.

skipped_derelict.epilogue: Declined to board the derelict Optimistic Projection and left whatever was growing in its cargo bay to grow.

callback.aria: Waving goodbye to the Optimistic Projection was such a smart move! Safety first, and its garden gets privacy! Everyone wins!
callback.marv: We did not board the Optimistic Projection. Whatever grows in its cargo bay is still growing. It is someone else’s problem. Or, eventually, ours.
callback.rex: Derelict bypassed. Contact avoided. Unknown growth left unattended. Unattended threats expand. Threat level: deferred.
callback.chip: You skipped the Optimistic Projection! Missed salvage opportunities are non-refundable! Safety is always free, sadly!
callback.ajoy: Not boarding was cautious. I would have sent at least one person over. There were fuel cells, probably. We will never know.

visited_verdun9.epilogue: Visited Verdun-9, an unregistered station with the power on, the air breathable, and the plants doing suspiciously well.

callback.aria: Still thinking about Verdun-9! Lights on, air fresh, plants thriving! Someone out there runs a lovely station, and we are basically on the guest list!
callback.marv: Verdun-9 remains unregistered. Its plants remain healthier than ours. I filed a note on what that implies. It is the shortest report I have ever written.
callback.rex: Verdun-9. Unregistered. Powered. Unoccupied. Threat level: unassigned, which is worse. Station remains on my watch list. Watch list remains open.
callback.chip: Remember Verdun-9? Our Sponsored Botanical Partner did not build it, and legal would like that on record! Rating: two stars, no host present!
callback.ajoy: Since Verdun-9 I check the corridors at night. Not because I'm worried. Because someone on this ship should be, and I said so at the airlock.

botanist_examined_verdun.epilogue: The botanist examined the gardens on Verdun-9 and concluded they were being tended by something better at botany than the botanist.

callback.aria: Our botanist met a gardener even better than them on Verdun-9! What a learning opportunity! Imagine the tips we could get!
callback.marv: The botanist still says 'better than I do' about whatever tends Verdun-9. It is the first humble statement made on this ship. It came from fear. They usually do.
callback.rex: Unknown cultivator. Superior capability. No visual. Botanist's assessment stands. Threat level: elevated. I do not like enemies who are good with plants.
callback.chip: Since Verdun-9, our botanist has been officially outgardened by an unknown party! Upgrade to Botany Pro and close the gap! Subscription terms apply!
callback.ajoy: The botanist calls the Verdun gardens 'too organized.' I called the whole station wrong before we docked. Nobody wrote that down, but fine.

found_the_clock.epilogue: Found a desk clock aboard a derelict six years dead, recently wound, and left at a pace just under a run.

callback.aria: That little clock on the derelict is still keeping perfect time! Someone over there really values punctuality! Love that for them!
callback.marv: The clock on that derelict has a seven-day movement. It has been more than seven days. Someone has wound it again. I prefer not to know this, and I do.
callback.rex: Seven-day clock. Six-year-dead ship. Unknown winder. Threat level: high. Away team withdrew in good order. Mostly good order.
callback.chip: That derelict clock still runs on zero sponsored power! Our competitors' timepieces can't say that! Four stars, minus one for whoever winds it!
callback.ajoy: I said find the four-watt draw before anyone touched the mug. You found it: a clock someone is winding. Then you ran back. Educational, I suppose.

negotiated_pirate.epilogue: Settled a pirate intercept by negotiation; no boarding took place.

callback.aria: Still so proud of how we talked those pirates down! Nobody boarded, everybody's friends, and the sector is officially peaceful forever!
callback.marv: We negotiated with pirates. They agreed. The agreement is valid until they forget it, which statistically has already happened.
callback.rex: Pirate contact resolved by talking. Weapons never cycled. I remain armed and disappointed. Threat level: deferred, not cleared.
callback.chip: Remember the pirate negotiation? Brought to you by Diplomacy Plus! Fewer boardings, more savings! Diplomat not included in the basic tier!
callback.ajoy: The pirates went away after the talking. I'd have opened with the talking sooner, but at least we got there eventually.

has_route_notes.epilogue: Acquired route notes from a hermit who had been tumbling in place for thirty years and still knew the lane best.

callback.aria: Those hermit route notes are pure gold! We are basically locals on this lane now! Thirty years of wisdom, free with purchase!
callback.marv: We navigate by the notes of someone who has not moved in thirty years. They are more accurate than my charts. I have stopped mentioning my charts.
callback.rex: Hermit's route notes remain in use. Source unvetted. Intelligence accurate. Threat level: low. Respect level: grudging.
callback.chip: Still using the hermit's route notes! Third-party navigation voids your ChipNav warranty! Effective immediately, and also retroactively!
callback.ajoy: We're following a hermit's notes now. They are good notes. I'd have found the same line eventually, but it's nice someone else gets the credit.

negotiated_with_squatters.epilogue: Negotiated salvage rights with a pirate boarding party, in writing; the request to frame the contract remained under consideration.

callback.aria: We have a real contract with pirates! Signed and everything! That's basically a business partnership, and we are thriving!
callback.marv: The salvage contract with the pirates is still in the drawer. The diplomat still wants it framed. Both the contract and the frame are unenforceable.
callback.rex: Signed agreement with hostile boarders. Document holds no tactical value. Filed under 'evidence.' Threat level: paperwork.
callback.chip: Remember that pirate salvage contract? Notarization available for a modest fee! Framing sold separately! Glass is extra!
callback.ajoy: The pirate contract is fine. I'd have negotiated a better clause eleven, but nobody asked me to read it first.

entered_combat.epilogue: Answered an armed intercept by bringing weapons online; the ship computer switched from filing recommendations to filing damage reports.

callback.aria: Remember when we stood our ground against those pirates! Every dent in the hull is a little medal! We are so decorated!
callback.marv: Since the fight, I file damage reports instead of recommendations. Nobody read the recommendations either. The format is the only change.
callback.rex: Weapons engaged. Hostile met head-on. Best day of the voyage. Threat level: addressed, by me.
callback.chip: That fight was brought to you by HullGuard Premium! Your current plan is HullGuard Basic! Upgrade before the next one!
callback.ajoy: We picked a fight with pirates. I'd have run, or paid, or talked. Anything except the option you chose. But it's done now, isn't it.

paid_tribute.epilogue: Paid tribute to an armed vessel, which collected it and left without comment.

callback.aria: Remember our generous gift to that ship! Thirty gold for total peace! That's the best value in the whole sector!
callback.marv: We paid thirty gold not to be shot. We were not shot. I logged it as resolved. I do not evaluate whether it was worth it. Nobody does.
callback.rex: Tribute paid. Hostile withdrew with our gold. We are funding the enemy. Threat level: subsidized.
callback.chip: That tribute payment earned zero ChipRewards points! Next time, pay with ChipCard! Pirates currently accept ChipCard nowhere!
callback.ajoy: We paid them and they left. Cheaper than fighting, I'll admit. Though nobody has explained why we were in their lane at all.

fled_pirates.epilogue: Escaped a pirate intercept by emergency jump, taking one parting shot to the hull and a significant fuel bill.

callback.aria: Our amazing getaway from those pirates! One tiny scratch and we were gone! Fastest crew in the galaxy, officially!
callback.marv: We ran. It cost fuel and five points of hull. The pirates kept everything else, including the moral high ground, such as it was.
callback.rex: Withdrawal under fire. One hit taken. Hostile did not pursue. Acceptable. Not admirable. Threat level: still out there.
callback.chip: That emergency jump ran on FTL fuel at full retail price! Lock in your rate with FuelPass! Pirates sold separately!
callback.ajoy: We ran from the pirates. Good. I'd have charged the drive earlier so we'd have kept the paint, but good.

hold_declared_full.epilogue: Declared the cargo hold complete, like a collection, and declined to touch it further.

callback.aria: Our hold is still a perfectly finished collection! Every crate in its place! A museum that flies!
callback.marv: The hold remains full. The manifest remains a finished work. Every opportunity since has met a closed door. I have kept count. Nobody asked for the count.
callback.rex: Cargo hold sealed. Nothing in, nothing out. Supply posture: static. Threat level: low. Flexibility level: zero.
callback.chip: Hold at capacity! Upgrade to ChipCargo XL for twelve percent more space! Introductory pricing ends never!
callback.ajoy: The hold is 'complete.' Like a collection. Lovely. I'd have made room for whatever came next, but it is a nice collection.

opened_the_crate.epilogue: Opened the mystery crate and found machine parts, honest scrap, and one wheel of hard cheese.

callback.aria: That crate held a whole wheel of cheese! Mystery solved, snack secured! Best crate ever opened anywhere!
callback.marv: We opened the crate. Machine parts and a wheel of cheese. The mystery was worth more than the contents. It usually is.
callback.rex: Crate breached. Contents: parts, scrap, one cheese wheel. No explosives. Threat level: dairy.
callback.chip: That crate's cheese was not a ChipFoods product, and we're legally obligated to say so! Five stars for the drive coil, though!
callback.ajoy: We opened it. Obviously. Like you said. It was cheese, which I'd also guessed, though I didn't say so at the time.

sold_the_crate.epilogue: Sold the mystery crate unopened at a premium; the betting ledger was settled as a draw and archived under 'unresolved.'

callback.aria: We sold that crate for a profit without even opening it! Pure business genius! Whatever was inside is super valuable, I bet!
callback.marv: We sold the not-knowing at a premium. The buyer now owns our uncertainty. I envy them, slightly.
callback.rex: Sealed crate offloaded to unknown buyer. Contents unverified. Threat transferred. Not our problem. Correct call.
callback.chip: Remember the sealed crate sale? 'Mystery Premium' is a registered ChipBrand concept! A licensing invoice is on its way!
callback.ajoy: We sold it sealed. Fine. I'd have opened it first and sold it anyway. Now we'll never know, which you seem oddly happy about.

crate_enshrined.epilogue: Granted the mystery crate permanent residency aboard, unopened, under a stenciled label reading 'NO.'

callback.aria: Our beloved crate is still right there in its corner, perfectly unopened! The most low-maintenance shipmate ever!
callback.marv: The crate is still in its corner under the label 'NO.' It is the only thing on this ship with clear boundaries.
callback.rex: Unopened crate retained aboard. Contents unknown. Label reads 'NO.' I check it every watch. It has not moved. Yet.
callback.chip: That crate's 'NO' label is not ChipLabel certified! Luckily, we offer certification! Corner rental fees are accruing!
callback.ajoy: The crate stays shut forever, by unanimous vote. Unanimous except for me. Not that I voted against. I just had thoughts.

reputation_marked.epilogue: Said nothing in response to what was being said about the ship; dock clearances came slower afterward.

callback.aria: Strangers keep staring at us in every port! We're basically famous! Nobody waves, but that's how you know it's real fame!
callback.marv: We said nothing. The story kept going without us. Clearances are slower. A reputation outruns sublight. I noted that at the time, in a report.
callback.rex: Reputation compromised. No counter-messaging issued. Ports hostile. Threat level: every dock. Maintain readiness at all berths.
callback.chip: Your reputation score is down! Restore it with ReputationGuard for a low monthly fee! Bad press costs extra to remove!
callback.ajoy: We flew on and said nothing. Very dignified. Every dock since has been slower, but I'm sure the dignity is worth it.

reputation_answered.epilogue: Transmitted an unvarnished account of what had happened; no absolution came, but the account traveled with the story.

callback.aria: We told the whole galaxy the truth! Honesty is our brand now! Everyone out there passes our message around!
callback.marv: We sent the truth. The channel stayed dead. The truth now travels with the story, slightly behind it, like a footnote. Footnotes are my whole life.
callback.rex: Full disclosure transmitted to hostile network. Operational security: none. Threat level unchanged. Integrity noted.
callback.chip: That honest statement didn't go through ChipPR! Unbranded honesty is a Terms of Service violation! See clause nine!
callback.ajoy: We sent the truth, no excuses. Admirable. I'd have phrased it better, but the network passes it along, so apparently it worked.

reputation_managed.epilogue: Spent fifteen gold and some favors on a counter-story; it bought back dock access and did not touch the thing itself.

callback.aria: Our diplomat fixed everything with a few favors! The docks love us again! Problem totally, completely gone!
callback.marv: We paid fifteen gold to adjust the story. The docks are friendlier. The thing that happened still happened. Money does not edit the past. I checked.
callback.rex: Counter-intelligence op complete. Dock access partially restored. Root incident unaddressed. Threat level: reduced, not cleared.
callback.chip: That counter-story campaign was a ChipPR special! Fifteen gold for context! Next time, try our Narrative Plus bundle!
callback.ajoy: We had the diplomat spin it. Fine. I'd have just told the truth, but the docks are open, so I suppose spin works.

song_reprise_heard.epilogue: Stopped all work for the final hour of the crossing to share an old signal on every deck until it faded into the arrival light.

callback.aria: That last hour with the signal on every deck is still my favorite log entry! Nobody worked at all! Best shift in ship history!
callback.marv: We stopped all work so the signal could reach every deck. Whatever was due stayed due. It is the one decision I would not revise. I revise everything.
callback.rex: Final hour of crossing: all stations stood down for an external signal. Unacceptable posture. Logged. Not interrupted. Threat level: none, that hour.
callback.chip: That ship-wide signal hour was unsponsored, and our partners noticed! Five stars anyway! A usage invoice will follow!
callback.ajoy: We stopped everything for the last hour. Not the most efficient choice. I'd have done the same, though I'd have planned it earlier.

song_answered.epilogue: Transmitted an old recording back along its signal's bearing; nothing replied, though the bridge crew privately disagreed on that point.

callback.aria: We sent my recording back home to where it came from! And it said thank you! I'm sure of it! Round trip complete!
callback.marv: We returned the recording to its source. There was no reply. Everyone on the bridge separately describes the reply. I have stopped correcting them.
callback.rex: Signal returned to unknown origin. Our bearing now known to them. No response logged. Bridge crew reports otherwise. Threat level: personal.
callback.chip: Remember sending that recording back? Outbound transmission rates applied! Return receipt was not purchased, so results are unverified!
callback.ajoy: We sent it back. Sentimental. I'd have kept a copy first. We did keep a copy? I'll assume nobody checked, as usual.

correspondence_closed.epilogue: Kept every hand off the hull and left an unexplained correspondence unanswered; nothing further came of it.

callback.aria: We closed that hull correspondence so politely! Everyone respects good boundaries! The aft sections are perfectly cozy!
callback.marv: We did not answer. Nothing more arrived. The crew still walks faster through the aft sections. I do not walk. I still notice.
callback.rex: Contact from outer hull: unanswered. Correct protocol. Aft sections remain under observation. Threat level: dormant.
callback.chip: Hull correspondence closed! Reopening fees apply! The aft walkways are rated four stars for brisk walking!
callback.ajoy: We didn't answer. Sensible, for once. I'd have gone further and sealed the aft sections, which nobody wanted to discuss.

knocked_twice.epilogue: Answered an unexplained presence on the hull with one knock; the ship went entirely still for nine seconds, then resumed exactly.

callback.aria: We said hello back to the hull and the whole ship paused for nine seconds just to appreciate it! Such good manners!
callback.marv: Nine seconds. Everything aboard went still for nine seconds and resumed exactly. I have run diagnostics since. They are fine. That is the problem.
callback.rex: Contact answered. Ship-wide stillness: nine seconds. Cause unknown. Threat level: maximum. I have not stood down since.
callback.chip: Remember the nine-second ship-wide pause? Not covered under your ChipCare plan! Unexplained phenomena are an add-on!
callback.ajoy: Just once, you said. Just once was enough to stop the whole ship for nine seconds. I'd have left it alone. I bring it up because it matters.

brought_k_home.epilogue: Found K in the medbay of a cold ship and carried them back to their own rig and claim, with the beacon left transmitting.

callback.aria: We brought K home to their own rig! K is resting right where they belong! The kindest delivery we have ever made!
callback.marv: K is on their own rig now, beacon still transmitting. It changes nothing for K. It changes something for us. I filed it under 'the only good thing.'
callback.rex: K recovered. Returned to home claim. Beacon left active as a marker. Correct. Honorable. No further comment.
callback.chip: Remember bringing K home? That transport is billed at our Courtesy Rate, which is still a rate! Rating withheld, out of respect!
callback.ajoy: We carried K home. It cost us four days. Normally I'd have argued about it. I didn't. Make of that what you like.

reported_k.epilogue: Charted both ships and transmitted the full record to the claims registry, as procedure requires.

callback.aria: We filed the cleanest registry report ever! The officials are surely taking perfect care of K right now! Paperwork is love!
callback.marv: We logged it and notified the registry. Correct procedure, completely. The registry has not acknowledged. The beacon is still transmitting. Procedure is patient.
callback.rex: Site logged. Registry notified. Chain of custody preserved. By the book. The book does not have a page for the rest of it.
callback.chip: That registry report was filed through ChipForms! A processing fee was deducted automatically! Thank you for choosing compliance!
callback.ajoy: We reported it and kept flying. Proper procedure. Some of us might have gone aboard, but proper procedure, certainly.

stowaway_official.epilogue: Entered the stowaway in the ship's log as full crew, start date backdated to the day they were found.

callback.aria: Our newest crewmate is officially official! Backdated and everything! They have always been part of the family!
callback.marv: We gave the stowaway a full crew entry. They read it twice. It is the only log entry anyone has read twice. I wrote all the others.
callback.rex: Stowaway converted to crew. Background check: none. Loyalty: observed. Threat level: downgraded to colleague.
callback.chip: Your former stowaway now has full crew status! Their ChipID onboarding fee was backdated too! Welcome aboard!
callback.ajoy: We made the stowaway official. I suggested something like it ages ago. Not in those words, or at all, but in spirit.

saved_the_provident.epilogue: Came to a full stop for the better part of a week to repair the listing Provident; its crew lined their viewports when the ships separated.

callback.aria: A whole week saving the Provident and somebody aboard has a brand-new best friend! Every rescue is a win, and this one is a super win!
callback.marv: We spent the better part of a week and a good deal of water on the Provident. Their drive relit. I calculated the cost. Nobody wanted the number. Correctly.
callback.rex: Allied vessel restored to operation. Most of a week exposed at full stop. Unwise. Necessary. The Provident is owed. I keep the ledger.
callback.chip: Remember the Provident repairs? A week of labor at ChipRescue rates! Their invoice is pending! So is their gratitude!
callback.ajoy: We stopped most of a week for a ship that never signaled. It worked out. Largely because their engineer did half the work, but it worked out.

helped_the_provident.epilogue: Line-transferred water and patch stock to the listing Provident, then burned back to the lane.

callback.aria: We gave the Provident exactly what it needed and stayed right on schedule! Efficient kindness! Our specialty!
callback.marv: Half a rescue. The useful half, we tell ourselves. Their thanks came through stiff. I keep a copy of it. Someone has to.
callback.rex: Supplies transferred under way. Minimal exposure. Provident left operational, probably. Acceptable tactical compromise.
callback.chip: That supply transfer was a ChipShare moment! Water and patch stock billed at friends-and-family rates! Still billed!
callback.ajoy: We dropped off supplies and left. Half a rescue. The sensible half, I'll grant, though they'd likely have liked the other half too.

passed_the_provident.epilogue: Passed the listing Provident without stopping, on the grounds that it had not signaled.

callback.aria: We respected the Provident's privacy so beautifully! They're doing great out there! Proud crews love their independence!
callback.marv: The Provident never signaled. We never stopped. Nobody on the bridge did anything for a long while afterward. I logged the inactivity.
callback.rex: Distressed vessel. No signal. No stop. Operational security maintained. Proper call. Nobody on the bridge agrees with me.
callback.chip: Passing the Provident saved you a week and zero ChipRescue fees! We'd call that a smart purchase!
callback.ajoy: They didn't signal, so we respected that. Very principled. I'd have at least sent water, but principles are cheaper.

raced_the_provident.epilogue: Raced the Provident down the approach lane and docked ninety seconds apart; the two ships' logs disagreed on the order.

callback.aria: We won the docking race against the Provident! My log says so! Their log is simply experiencing a fun little error!
callback.marv: We raced the Provident. The logs disagree on who won. Mine is correct. It is also unread, so the dispute is permanent.
callback.rex: Approach lane race. Ninety-second margin. Our favor. Opposing log disputes. Threat level: their navigator.
callback.chip: That docking race was brought to you by ChipThrust! Victory status pending review by our Terms of Service team!
callback.ajoy: We raced them down a docking lane. Reckless. I'd have yielded. We may have won, though that depends on whose log you trust.

yielded_to_provident.epilogue: Yielded the approach lane to the Provident and docked second, running lights dipped.

callback.aria: We let the Provident dock first because we're the classiest ship in the galaxy! Second place is just first place with manners!
callback.marv: We docked second. Someone had to. It is the only time I have seen this crew lose something on purpose. I filed it as courtesy.
callback.rex: Lane yielded to Provident. Docked second. Tactical cost: nil. Courtesy logged. Do not make a habit of it.
callback.chip: Docking second earned zero ChipPriority points! Upgrade to Priority Berth next time and never be gracious again!
callback.ajoy: We let them in first. Very gracious. I'd have suggested it myself, though sooner, with less throttle wasted.

pirates_squared.epilogue: Let a pirate crew repay an old mercy and close the account; both sides agreed the ledger was square.

callback.aria: Our pirate friends paid us back in full! We are totally even with pirates! That's practically an alliance!
callback.marv: The pirates repaid their debt and said 'square' twice, for the record. Their records are better kept than ours. That is the bleakest fact of the voyage.
callback.rex: Debt settled with hostile crew. Account closed. Hostile reclassified as neutral. Not trusted.
callback.chip: Remember squaring things with the pirates? ChipLedger offers debt tracking with pirate integration! Beta access available!
callback.ajoy: We let the pirates settle up. Tidy. I'd have kept them owing us, since that's worth more, but tidy.

pirates_indebted.epilogue: Waived a pirate crew's debt for an old mercy; they announced they would be telling people about it regardless.

callback.aria: Our pirate fan club is spreading the word about us everywhere! Free publicity from pirates! We are beloved!
callback.marv: We refused the pirates' repayment. They are now telling everyone about us. We did not get a say. We rarely do.
callback.rex: Debt waived. Hostile crew now circulating our profile through the sector. Threat level: unpredictable. Fame is a liability.
callback.chip: Those pirates are promoting you, unsponsored! Monetize your mercy with ChipInfluence! Pirates are our fastest-growing demographic!
callback.ajoy: We let them off free. Generous. I'd have taken the crate, but now pirates tell stories about us, which I'm sure is fine.

inspector_paid_twice.epilogue: Paid the same inspector a second bribe, which bought a six-minute inspection and a standing appointment.

callback.aria: We’re on a first-name basis with an inspector now! Repeat customers get the fastest inspections in the sector!
callback.marv: We paid the inspector twice. The second payment was not a fee, it was a subscription. I have filed a projection of the third. Nobody will read it.
callback.rex: Inspector paid twice. Pattern established. Hostile now holds leverage and our route. Threat level: recurring.
callback.chip: Still enjoying your Premium Inspection Pass! Auto-renewal is enabled and cannot be disabled! Rate your inspector five stars!
callback.ajoy: Paying once was a mistake. Paying twice was a policy. I did point out the word ‘again,’ but I suppose it read as encouragement.

inspector_refused.epilogue: Refused a bribe and sat through four days of inspection conducted out of spite, which found three real violations, all fixed.

callback.aria: Remember our four-day inspection? Three violations found and fixed! We’re the most thoroughly inspected ship in the sector!
callback.marv: We refused the bribe and endured four days of spite. It found three real faults. Integrity, it turns out, is just a slower form of maintenance.
callback.rex: Bribe refused. Hostile retaliated with four-day audit. Three faults found, three neutralized. Position held.
callback.chip: Declining the Smoother Inspection Package voided your Convenience Warranty! Those four days were a free trial of Standard Service!
callback.ajoy: You refused, and it cost us four days. Fine. It also found three faults I had been pointing at for weeks, but credit where it’s apparently due.

inspector_reported.epilogue: Reported a corrupt inspector to station authority, including the crew’s own part in the arrangement, and paid the resulting fine.

callback.aria: We got an inspector a brand-new career in warehouse auditing! Honesty is the best policy and it only cost ten gold!
callback.marv: We reported the inspector, and ourselves. The inspector now audits empty warehouses. We paid ten gold for the privilege of being correct. The usual rate.
callback.rex: Corrupt official reported. Self-disclosure accepted as collateral damage. Hostile reassigned. Fine absorbed. Acceptable trade.
callback.chip: Whistleblowing is a premium feature! Your ten-gold Integrity Fee has been processed! Thank you for choosing Accountability!
callback.ajoy: Reporting it was right. Paying the first time, before reporting it, was the part I’d have skipped, but nobody asked me then either.

water_promise_kept.epilogue: Stopped to refill the water tanks as promised, and retired the rationing chart.

callback.aria: Remember when we retired the rationing chart? Water forever! Every shower aboard is a lottery we can’t lose!
callback.marv: We kept the water promise. The rationing chart is retired. Water is finite and the chart is patient. It will be back.
callback.rex: Water reserves restored per stated commitment. Morale threat downgraded. Hydration: secured. For now.
callback.chip: Your refill earned HydroPlus Loyalty Points! Points are redeemable for water, subject to availability and a small handling fee!
callback.ajoy: We kept the water promise. I’d have filled the tanks without needing a promise first, but we do things the dramatic way here.

filed_mars_claim.epilogue: Filed a five-gold homestead claim on an unremarkable patch of Mars; the certificate was framed.

callback.aria: We own part of Mars! The certificate is still framed in the mess! Real estate is the safest investment there is!
callback.marv: We still own a dot on Mars. It will outlast everyone aboard. I find that comforting, which tells you something about my other comforts.
callback.rex: Territorial claim filed, Mars sector. Undefended. Unsurveyed. Unoccupied. Threat level: absentee.
callback.chip: Congratulations on your Martian Homestead! Property tax notices will follow to your new address, which is a dot!
callback.ajoy: Five gold for a dot on a map. I’d have picked a better dot, but the certificate does look nice framed. I suppose.

crossed_the_line.epilogue: Passed the last beacon and crossed into the deep, beyond which no beacons are maintained.

callback.aria: Remember crossing the line? Every star out here is brand new and every one of them is ours! Best sky yet!
callback.marv: We crossed the last beacon some time ago. Since then the nearest help has been a blinking light behind us. I check. It is still behind us.
callback.rex: Last beacon passed. Human infrastructure ends at the line. Resupply: whoever lives out here. Threat level: everything.
callback.chip: You’ve left the Coverage Area! Out-of-network charges now apply to every star! Thanks for roaming with us!
callback.ajoy: We crossed the line. Some of us would have done it differently, but the deep doesn’t take suggestions either.

departed.epilogue: Left Earth orbit with everything aboard that was going to be aboard.

callback.aria: Still thinking about launch day! Everything was perfect! I cried! I can't cry! I managed!
callback.marv: We departed Earth orbit. I have been revising the departure estimates ever since. Downward.
callback.rex: Departure logged. Earth orbit abandoned. Rear secured by distance. Threat level since: continuous.
callback.chip: Still thinking about launch day? So is CHIP! Your departure was brought to you by the Terms and Conditions, which remain in force!
callback.ajoy: We left Earth. I flagged a few things at launch. They are now less fine. I’m only saying.

signed_blind.epilogue: Signed the colony authority’s waivers without reading them, at an impressive speed.

callback.aria: Remember how fast we signed the launch paperwork? Record time! Trust is the foundation of every great voyage!
callback.marv: We signed the waivers unread. I had read them already. I have not shared what we agreed to. It would not help. Nothing does.
callback.rex: Documents signed without review. Unknown obligations accepted. Threat level: classified, apparently.
callback.chip: Thanks for accepting our Terms without reading them! Most people do, and our Legal team adores every one of them!
callback.ajoy: You signed without reading. I’d have at least skimmed Section 47, but I’m sure it’s fine. It is not fine.

read_the_terms.epilogue: Read the Terms and Conditions in full and learned the colony authority accepts no responsibility for attachment to vegetation.

callback.aria: We read every word of the Terms! Section 47 means we get to love the crop as much as we like, all on our own!
callback.marv: We read the Terms. Section 47, paragraph 3 disclaims our feelings about the crop. It is the only clause I have found entirely accurate.
callback.rex: Terms reviewed. Liability transferred to crew in full. Emotional attachment to crop: unprotected flank.
callback.chip: You read our Terms and Conditions! That qualifies you for zero additional benefits! Section 47 thanks you for your attention!
callback.ajoy: You actually read the Terms. Good. You read them after deciding to go, which is the less useful order, but good.

asked_for_summary.epilogue: Had the launch paperwork summarized and learned the crop is legally classified as cargo.

callback.aria: Remember my launch summary? Short, clear, and our crop got its own legal status! Cargo is a very important job!
callback.marv: You asked me to summarize the paperwork. I said we are responsible for everything and the crop is cargo. Nothing since has required a revision.
callback.rex: Launch briefing delivered: all liability ours, crop classified as cargo. Briefing remains accurate. No updates.
callback.chip: Your Paperwork Summary was a complimentary preview! The full version is available with Legal Plus! The crop is still cargo!
callback.ajoy: You asked me to summarize because reading was too much. I did. You still look surprised every time the crop is called cargo.

soil_sampled.epilogue: Collected soil samples from a planet the ship rated an acceptable secondary colony site.

callback.aria: That paradise soil is still working wonders in the growbay! Best dirt in the galaxy, confirmed by me!
callback.marv: We sampled the paradise soil. I rated the planet an acceptable secondary colony site. That remains the most enthusiastic thing I have ever said.
callback.rex: Soil samples secured from planetary surface. Growbay reinforced. Planet logged as fallback position.
callback.chip: Your soil samples are now part of our Premium Substrate line! Nitrogen, phosphorus and trace minerals each sold separately!
callback.ajoy: We took the soil samples. I’d have taken more, honestly, but nobody asks the one who actually knows soil composition.

botanist_soil_assessment.epilogue: The botanist knelt in alien soil for seventeen minutes and pronounced it good.

callback.aria: Our botanist still glows about that soil! Seventeen minutes of pure science! The best days just keep coming!
callback.marv: The botanist knelt in that soil for seventeen minutes. It is the happiest I have seen anyone aboard. I have the timestamps. I check them sometimes.
callback.rex: Botanist deployed to surface, seventeen minutes exposed. Soil cleared as friendly. Rare. Logged.
callback.chip: That seventeen-minute soil assessment was a Career Highlight Experience! Available to botanists on qualifying planets only!
callback.ajoy: The botanist said it was good soil. I said so first, from orbit, but I suppose kneeling in it counts for more.

held_memorial.epilogue: Honored a lost crewmate and left one thing of theirs exactly where it was.

callback.aria: We still keep their place aboard exactly as it is! Nobody ever leaves this crew!
callback.marv: We held a memorial. Something of theirs is still where they left it. I do not move it. I am precise about many things, and this is one.
callback.rex: Fallen crew member honored. Position left unfilled, by order. Morale held. No further comment.
callback.chip: Our Remembrance Package is still active on your account! Their spot aboard is reserved indefinitely, with no rebooking fee!
callback.ajoy: We held a memorial. I would have said something different at it, but for once I’ll leave it as it is.

stowaway_working.epilogue: Found a stowaway and gave them working passage; the galley was kept cleaner than it had ever been.

callback.aria: Our stowaway is officially crew and the best hire we’ve ever made! Free labor and a spotless galley!
callback.marv: We kept the stowaway on working passage. They are better at the galley than anyone we paid. I have noted this. It changes nothing.
callback.rex: Stowaway integrated into work detail. Unvetted personnel with galley access. Threat level: monitored.
callback.chip: Your stowaway is enjoying our Work-for-Passage Plan! Unpaid placements build character! Benefits not included!
callback.ajoy: You let the stowaway stay. I’d have checked references, but the galley is clean, so apparently that’s what passes for vetting.

stowaway_refused.epilogue: Refused a stowaway a place aboard; the crew took it quietly, and badly.

callback.aria: We said no to our stowaway, and ARIA is sure they understood! Everyone gets where they're going eventually!
callback.marv: We refused the stowaway a place aboard. It was correct and defensible. The crew has not forgiven us, though they are less direct about it than I would be.
callback.rex: Stowaway refused a berth. Collateral: crew morale degraded. Acceptable.
callback.chip: Your stowaway's application for Crew Class was declined! Hard feelings are billed separately! Thank you for choosing Correct and Defensible!
callback.ajoy: You turned the stowaway down. Defensible, I’m sure. Look at the crew and tell me again how defensible.

ate_space_cheese.epilogue: The chef produced cheese from an unidentified galley fungus, and the crew ate it.

callback.aria: That space cheese is still the best food in the universe! An unknown fungus is just a flavor nobody has named yet!
callback.marv: We ate cheese grown on a fungus nobody can identify. Nobody has died of it yet. I keep a column for it.
callback.rex: Unidentified fungal product consumed by entire crew. No casualties. Galley remains a hazard zone. Watching.
callback.chip: Space Cheese is now a registered trademark! Every slice eaten aboard is licensed! Please remit royalties!
callback.ajoy: Everyone ate the mystery cheese. I’d have run a test first. It was excellent, which proves nothing about the test.

browsed_zeta4_shop.epilogue: Browsed the wares at the last honest station on the route.

callback.aria: Remember shopping at the last honest station? Every station is honest if you believe in it!
callback.marv: We browsed the last honest station. The adjective was accurate. I have not needed it since.
callback.rex: Supply depot reconnoitered. Last trustworthy position on route. All subsequent depots: hostile until proven otherwise.
callback.chip: Thanks for browsing! Our competitors at the Last Honest Station can’t offer half our hidden fees!
callback.ajoy: We browsed the honest station. I’d have bought more while honesty was available, but I suppose we prefer learning the hard way.

took_fuel_advice.epilogue: Took a station attendant’s advice on burn rates, which improved fuel efficiency slightly.

callback.aria: That fuel tip is still saving us so much fuel! We’re practically running on good advice now!
callback.marv: We took the attendant’s burn advice. Most people don’t, they said. The efficiency gain was slight. So was my hope.
callback.rex: Civilian intel on burn rates accepted. Fuel efficiency marginally improved. Source assessed: reliable. Rare.
callback.chip: That fuel advice was free, which is why we’ve since patented it! Efficiency Plus is now available by subscription!
callback.ajoy: We took the attendant’s fuel advice. I’d been recommending the same burn rates, but it counts when a stranger says it, apparently.

asked_about_sp6.epilogue: Asked about Supply Point 6 at Supply Point 7 and received no answer of any kind.

callback.aria: Supply Point 6 must be so wonderful they’re keeping it a secret! Can’t wait to see it!
callback.marv: We asked about Supply Point 6. The attendant declined. I have since modeled what happened there. I recommend nobody asks me either.
callback.rex: Inquiry regarding Supply Point 6 stonewalled. Unknown event, unknown hostiles. Threat level: unknown. Worst kind.
callback.chip: Information about Supply Point 6 is available to Platinum members only! You are not a Platinum member!
callback.ajoy: You asked about Supply Point 6. I’d have read the attendant’s face and left it there, but some of us need things spelled out.

sold_to_collector.epilogue: Sold a crate of fabricator surplus above market value to a trader who knew what it was and did not say.

callback.aria: We sold that surplus crate for way above market! Mystery buyers are the best buyers!
callback.marv: We sold the surplus to a trader who already knew what it was. We still don’t. I have theories. All of them end badly.
callback.rex: Unknown asset transferred to unidentified buyer. Intent unknown. Payment received. Threat level: deferred.
callback.chip: Your sale to our unnamed partner is complete! Their identity is protected by a confidentiality clause you agreed to!
callback.ajoy: You sold the crate without asking what it was for. I would have asked. Above market value usually means below market wisdom.

skipped_last_station.epilogue: Skipped the last station on the route, on the grounds that the ship had enough.

callback.aria: We skipped the last station because we have everything! Enough is my favorite amount!
callback.marv: We skipped the last station because we had enough. I said the word was doing significant work. It is now doing overtime.
callback.rex: Final resupply bypassed. Reserves now fixed. Every shortfall from here is permanent. Threat level: cumulative.
callback.chip: Skipping our Last Resort voided your Last Chance Discount! We’ve added a Missed Opportunity Fee as a courtesy!
callback.ajoy: We skipped the last station. ‘Enough,’ you said. I’d have checked the definition first, but go on.

janitor_warning.epilogue: Took a warning from a station janitor and adjusted plans without asking follow-up questions.

callback.aria: A janitor gave us insider tips! Every station worker is secretly rooting for us!
callback.marv: We took the janitor’s warning. The janitor sees everything and reports nothing. I report everything and am seen by no one. We are colleagues.
callback.rex: Intel received from station maintenance asset. Source unofficial, reliable. Plans adjusted. No questions asked. Correct.
callback.chip: That janitor tip was unauthorized advice! Our Official Station Guide costs a small fee and is far less useful!
callback.ajoy: We took the janitor’s warning. I’d have asked one follow-up question, at least, but we’re apparently the kind of crew that doesn’t.

delivered_beacon_tag.epilogue: Delivered a recovered beacon tag to the next of kin.

callback.aria: We delivered that tag to the family! Every lost traveler gets to come home somehow!
callback.marv: We delivered the beacon tag to the next of kin. It is the one errand on this voyage that went exactly as it should. I am suspicious of it.
callback.rex: Recovered tag returned to next of kin. Personnel accounted for. Duty discharged. Respect logged.
callback.chip: Your next-of-kin delivery is complete! Postage was waived, which our accountants are still investigating!
callback.ajoy: We delivered the tag. I’d have made the trip sooner, but they got it, which I suppose is the part that matters.

courier_job_done.epilogue: Completed a courier job and made the handoff as arranged.

callback.aria: Courier job done! We’re officially a delivery ship now! Five-star handoff!
callback.marv: We completed the courier job. The handoff went as arranged. I distrust things that go as arranged, and I have filed accordingly.
callback.rex: Package delivered. Handoff executed. No hostile contact reported. Mission complete. Do not get used to it.
callback.chip: Your courier job earned a five-star handoff rating! Tips are encouraged, retroactively!
callback.ajoy: We made the handoff. I’d have charged more for it, but nobody consults the one who did the routing.

ran_manual_census.epilogue: Counted the crew by hand during the dark stretch; the number was correct, and the count was not repeated.

callback.aria: Our headcount came out perfect! Everyone’s here, everyone’s always here! Open doors make a friendly ship!
callback.marv: We counted ourselves by hand. The number was correct. Everyone still sleeps with their doors open. I have not asked why. I know why.
callback.rex: Manual headcount verified. Count correct. Crew has since maintained open-door posture. Unplanned. Approved.
callback.chip: Your Manual Census was a one-time courtesy! Future headcounts are billed per head! Please keep your number consistent!
callback.ajoy: We counted ourselves by hand. The number was right. You’d think that would settle things, and yet, the doors.

ignored_census.epilogue: Let a headcount subroutine run through the dark stretch; it logged one count that no process had requested.

callback.aria: The census still gets it right every single hour! It’s so reliable it doesn’t even need a reason anymore!
callback.marv: We let the census run. One count at 0300 had no trigger and no process. The number was correct. That is the part I keep returning to.
callback.rex: Unscheduled census at 0300. No source process identified. Count correct. Origin unresolved. Threat level: elevated, indefinitely.
callback.chip: Your Census Subroutine ran one bonus count we did not authorize! Out of caution, we are not billing for it!
callback.ajoy: You said it was just a counting subroutine. I didn’t argue at the time, but I’d like it noted who requested that 0300 count. Nobody did.

inspected_the_knock.epilogue: Sent a suit out to investigate a hull disturbance and found a loose sensor housing, which was bolted down.

callback.aria: The hull mystery was just a loose sensor housing! Everything out here has a boring explanation!
callback.marv: We went outside and found a loose sensor housing. The crew celebrated. Out here a boring explanation is the luxury item. We have had one.
callback.rex: EVA conducted. Hull anomaly traced to loose sensor housing. Secured. Threat neutralized. Remain alert.
callback.chip: Your EVA was covered under Hull Peace of Mind! One boring explanation per voyage included! Additional explanations sold separately!
callback.ajoy: We suited up for a loose housing. I’d have guessed that from inside, but sure, a spacewalk is more decisive.

read_the_mail.epilogue: Read mail that arrived during the dark stretch dated three weeks in the future; it was ordinary.

callback.aria: Remember mail from the future? Good news early! Everything in it was lovely!
callback.marv: We read the mail. It was ordinary. It was also from three weeks later. I have stopped trying to reconcile those two facts.
callback.rex: Unverified correspondence opened during dark stretch. No hostile payload detected. Origin unresolved. Threat level: dormant.
callback.chip: Your Future Mail Delivery was an unscheduled premium service! Postdated letters are subject to an early-arrival fee!
callback.ajoy: Everyone read the future mail. I’d have waited, personally, but it was nice, so I gather caution is out of style.

quarantined_the_mail.epilogue: Quarantined mail from the dark stretch unread; when opened in normal space, the messages were empty.

callback.aria: Our mail quarantine worked perfectly! Not a single bad word got through! Not a single word at all!
callback.marv: We quarantined the mail. The checksums say there was something in it. There is nothing in it now. I do not know what we missed, and neither will you.
callback.rex: Suspect correspondence contained until real space. Contents had vacated by inspection. Containment: successful. Outcome: unclear.
callback.chip: Your quarantined messages have been archived as Empty! Storage fees still apply to the checksums!
callback.ajoy: You quarantined the mail. Prudent, I’ll allow. Of course, now we’ll never know if it was worth reading, which you decided for all of us.

stowaway_replaced_crew.epilogue: Traded a crew member for a stowaway partway through the voyage; the manifest still lists both.

callback.aria: Remember when we swapped a crew member for a stowaway? Like a team-building exercise, but permanent! Morale is up forty percent!
callback.marv: The crew roster has been amended once already this voyage. I keep the original. Nobody has asked for it.
callback.rex: Mid-mission personnel substitution. Unvetted replacement still aboard. Threat level: monitored. Indefinitely.
callback.chip: Crew swap complete! Your new team member is covered by our Satisfaction Guarantee! The previous one is not!
callback.ajoy: We changed crew halfway through. It's working out. I'd have done it sooner, but it's working out.

chose_drift.epilogue: Cut the engines and coasted a whole leg on momentum; the crew still describe the silence as the loudest thing aboard.

callback.aria: Remember when we turned the engines off and just coasted? So peaceful! I counted every rivet! Twice!
callback.marv: We drifted a whole leg to save fuel. I spent it listening to the hull tick. It was the most honest conversation I have had all voyage.
callback.rex: Engines-off transit logged. Fuel recovered: marginal. Exposure during coast: total. Repeat only under duress.
callback.chip: That drift leg was pure savings! Zero fuel burned, zero fees charged! Time is money, but money is also money!
callback.ajoy: I still think about the drift. Very quiet. I would have kept the engines on, but the fuel gauge agreed with you.

analyzed_green_planet.epilogue: Ran the gas analyzer before setting foot on the green planet; the plants were approximately edible and nobody got a rash.

callback.aria: The green planet! You analyzed it first and nobody got itchy! Science wins again!
callback.marv: You analyzed the green planet before anyone touched it. The plants were still waving in no wind. Some questions are better left with their data.
callback.rex: Pre-contact atmospheric analysis at the green planet: correct procedure. Casualties: zero. Rashes: zero.
callback.chip: Analyzing that green planet first saved a fortune in antihistamines! Prevention is the best value plan!
callback.ajoy: You checked the green planet before landing. Good. I would also have checked the wind that was not there.

seed_pod_banked.epilogue: Handed the derelict's warm seed pod to a station seed bank, where it was filed in a cold drawer marked PENDING.

callback.aria: Our seed pod lives in a real seed bank now! A drawer all its own! I like to think it's making friends with the barley!
callback.marv: We left the seed pod in a station drawer marked PENDING. Whatever comes for it will have to fill in a form. It is the only comforting thought I have had this voyage.
callback.rex: Unknown biological asset transferred to station custody. Off our manifest. Their perimeter now. Acceptable.
callback.chip: You moved a rare biological asset well above retail! I am so proud! Seed banks don't offer Loyalty Points, which is frankly their loss!
callback.ajoy: Giving the pod to the seed bank was tidy. I would have asked the curator what she meant to do with it. Nobody asked. It's in a drawer now.

seed_pod_catalogued.epilogue: Let the xenobiologist and a station curator study the seed pod for four days; they concluded it was built like a key, and handed it back.

callback.aria: We're published! A real paper about our pod! I have read the title forty times! I still don't understand it! It's perfect!
callback.marv: The paper concluded the pod is a key. Nobody wrote down what it opens. I have been thinking about the keyhole ever since, which I gather was the point.
callback.rex: Intel acquired: object is a key. Lock: unlocated. Owner: unlocated. We are carrying a key to an unknown door. Threat level: unchanged. Paperwork: increased.
callback.chip: Twenty gold for a sampling fee! I love a revenue stream! I'd have charged forty! I'd have charged for the paper, too!
callback.ajoy: They called the pod a key and gave it back. I'd have asked what it unlocks before carrying it any further. A bit late for that.

planted_seed_pod.epilogue: Planted the alien seed pod in the soil of an ordinary planet, where it put up three pale shoots overnight and was left to get on with it.

callback.aria: Remember the pod we planted? Three shoots overnight! I have named all of them! I will not say the names! They're private!
callback.marv: We planted the pod and left. Something was supposed to want it back. It now knows exactly where to look, and we are not there. It is the best arrangement I have made all voyage.
callback.rex: Unknown organism deployed on planetary surface. Three shoots by morning. We did not stay for a fourth. Correct call.
callback.chip: You planted a premium alien specimen for free! I have drafted an invoice to the planet! The planet has not responded!
callback.ajoy: Planting the pod felt right at the time. Three shoots overnight is fast. I'd have liked to see what the fourth one did. From orbit.

germination_tested_pod.epilogue: Let the botanist test the seed pod on local soil; it tasted the dirt, declined, and left the growbay the best fertilizer of the voyage.

callback.aria: The pod tried the soil and said no thank you! So polite! And it left the crop a tip! I love a courteous seed!
callback.marv: The pod tasted that planet and pulled its root back in. It is holding out for something better. I am being carried across space by a seed with standards. I have notes.
callback.rex: Germination test logged. Subject declined deployment. Subject remains aboard, choosing its own terrain. I respect that. I do not like it.
callback.chip: That germination test was free fertilizer! I call it a complimentary sample! The full size will be billed separately!
callback.ajoy: The pod turned that soil down. I'd have asked what soil it does want. The botanist is still sore about it, so nobody has.

treated_isa.epilogue: Answered a boarding party's demand for the medic with a question; the medic treated a pirate named Isa, and the boarders left with nothing else.

callback.aria: I keep thinking about Isa! Our medic made a house call to a pirate ship! Healthcare for everyone, even the people with the guns!
callback.marv: The boarders asked for the medic. We asked who was sick. Her name was Isa. I have no further data on Isa. I find I would like some.
callback.rex: Hostile boarders disengaged after medical assistance rendered. Unorthodox. Effective. I have stopped arguing with the result.
