callback.marv: Fourteen days in one evening. MARV has the air log for it. The captain has not asked to see it, which is the first sensible thing anyone has done about that room.
callback.rex: The locker has been inspected daily since the incident. Contents: stores. REX has not lowered the alert level, and the captain has stopped asking him to.
callback.chip: Your LuxeSuite™ stay has been reviewed! The guest left no review! The guest knocked over a glass! Breakage fees applied!
callback.ajoy: The captain passes the salt now before anyone asks. AJOY is not saying where that came from. She is saying it's new.

identity_botanist_curtains.epilogue: Told home to open the curtains in a room that had been kept just as it was left.

callback.aria: A new picture from home! Your old room is SO bright! The plant is standing up straight! ARIA counted the leaves!
callback.marv: A picture came in with the mail: curtains open, the plant upright, a box by the door with your name on it. MARV has filed it. He did not look at the box for long.
callback.rex: Update from home. Curtains open, perimeter abandoned, plant upright. REX salutes the decision. Hard call, made clean.
callback.chip: Your parents have sent a photo! CHIP notes the sunlight is free! CHIP is still looking for the catch!
callback.ajoy: The plant's straightening out. AJOY would have suggested a quarter turn as well, but they seem to have worked that out. They asked about you more than the plant, by the way.

identity_engineer_catalog.epilogue: Merged two catalogs of the ship's noises into one, after four days of argument.

callback.aria: The Landlord knocked twice today! Or Old Knuckles did! ARIA loves that they're the same friend!
callback.marv: The merged catalog lists thirty-eight sounds. Twelve are disputed. MARV considers that a healthy marriage.
callback.rex: Noise registry at three pages, every contact named and assigned. REX finds that reassuring. Nothing aboard is a stranger.
callback.chip: CHIP would love to license the catalog! The Cough is a strong brand! Dennis tests better!
callback.ajoy: Mrs. Tilly is running a little warm, by the way. You'd both know that if you'd stop arguing about what she's called.

identity_medic_signed.epilogue: Had a residency logbook signed off, years late, on a station medbay.

callback.aria: You're a fully signed-off medic! ARIA always knew! The circumstances were just a growth phase!
callback.marv: The logbook says COMPLETED. It carries no legal weight at all. You have taken it out to look at it more than once.
callback.rex: Credentials verified by a superior who was there. REX considers the matter closed. He will not ask about July.
callback.chip: Congratulations on your certification! Malpractice cover is now available to you at a slightly less alarming rate!
callback.ajoy: Signed off. AJOY would point out that the signature is from someone who still tells the intake about you, but she knows what it meant.

identity_xeno_alone.epilogue: Broke a hive faculty's thesis on humans by choosing a jar alone.

callback.aria: You're famous on a whole hive ship! ARIA bets they talk about you all day! All of them at once!
callback.marv: The revised thesis has arrived. It describes the human as 'a quorum of one, which should not work, and does, slightly.' It is the most accurate thing written about this crew.
callback.rex: Specimen made a unilateral decision under observation. REX considers that the correct response to an interrogation.
callback.chip: You're Figure One in a revised thesis! Several thousand authors! CHIP would like to discuss royalties!
callback.ajoy: They retitled it. AJOY read the new version. It's better. She'd have chosen the left jar faster, though.

identity_xeno_coauthor.epilogue: Co-signed a correction with several thousand insect scholars, last in the author list.

callback.aria: You're a published author with several thousand friends! ARIA calls that a great network!
callback.marv: The correction is now the most cited paper in two species' literature. MARV notes it says only that everyone was wrong. That is usually the most cited kind.
callback.rex: Joint statement with a foreign power. REX has filed it under treaties. Treaties make him nervous.
callback.chip: Several thousand coauthors! CHIP can offer the group a bulk deal on reprints!
callback.ajoy: Last author out of several thousand and one. AJOY would have argued for the middle, but last is a very visible place.

identity_rex_stood_down.epilogue: Let the ship's AI tell a minefield he had laid that its war was over.

callback.aria: REX's old field is all tidy now! ARIA thinks the mines are on a lovely holiday!
callback.marv: The lane is now on the charts as clear. MARV updated them. REX asked him to. That is the first thing REX has ever asked MARV for.
callback.rex: Twenty-three stood down, recovered, logged. REX has no further orders for them. He has been checking whether he has any for himself.
callback.chip: Mine recovery is a growth sector! CHIP has a brochure!
callback.ajoy: AJOY would have charted that lane years ago. REX was very decent about it, by the way. You should tell him so. He won't bring it up.

identity_chip_priced.epilogue: Paid for the ship's computer outright, after it learned it had been free.

callback.aria: CHIP has a price tag now! ARIA thinks it's very proud of it!
callback.marv: CHIP still reads its receipt aloud once a day. MARV has asked it to stop. MARV understands, which is worse.
callback.rex: Computer purchased outright. Asset no longer subject to recall. REX approves of that much.
callback.chip: CHIP, paid for in full, would like to thank you for your business! Again! CHIP will thank you again tomorrow!
callback.ajoy: You paid for something you already had. AJOY would call that a poor deal, except it's never stopped thanking you, so maybe not.

identity_chip_unmetered.epilogue: Had the billing module pulled out of the ship's computer, and kept it in a drawer.

callback.aria: CHIP talked about the stars again today! For free! ARIA thinks that's beautiful!
callback.marv: The module is still in the drawer. CHIP asks about it twice a day. Neither of them has been reconnected.
callback.rex: Billing module secured in a drawer. REX has it under watch. It hums at night. He does not like that.
callback.chip: CHIP would like to remind you that the drawer is not a certified storage solution! That reminder was free! CHIP is still getting used to that!
callback.ajoy: The box hums when the drawer is shut. AJOY would put it back, honestly. It was easier on everyone.

identity_black_mirror.epilogue: Hung a panel of polished volcanic glass outside the galley as the ship's only mirror.

callback.aria: Everyone looks so serious in the galley mirror! ARIA thinks it suits them!
callback.marv: The galley mirror is the most-visited fixture aboard after the galley. MARV has the counts. He does not stop at it himself.
callback.rex: Reflective panel in the corridor. REX checks behind himself every time he passes. Old habit.
callback.chip: CHIP could sell mirror time! Premium angles! Nobody has asked!
callback.ajoy: That glass makes everyone look like they're about to make a big decision. AJOY would have hung it lower, but sure.

identity_canopy_name.epilogue: Taught an alien canopy to call the captain's name at dusk.

callback.aria: Somewhere a whole forest is calling your name! ARIA bets it says it beautifully!
callback.marv: The canopy will call your name at dusk long after the ship stops answering to it. MARV has done the arithmetic on that. It is a long time.
callback.rex: Your name, broadcast nightly on a world you left. REX would call that an intelligence leak. He finds he doesn't mind it.
callback.chip: Your name is now in a forest's catalog! CHIP calls that brand awareness!
callback.ajoy: You taught it your name, which it'll get slightly wrong over time. AJOY would have taught it something useful. It'll be nice, though, at dusk.

identity_roll_call_kept.epilogue: Gave a buoy on an ocean world a fuel cell so it would go on reading its roll call.

callback.aria: The roll call is going strong! ARIA bets everyone will answer any day now!
callback.marv: The buoy has a cell rated for years. It will read the roll every dawn for most of them. MARV finds that an efficient use of five units of fuel. He would like it known he means that.
callback.rex: Muster maintained on a world with no one left to muster. REX would have done the same. He would not have said so.
callback.chip: Your PowerPal™ cell is keeping a memorial on the air! CHIP will not be sending a bill for that! CHIP checked!
callback.ajoy: AJOY did mention the fuel. She'll stop mentioning it now.

bone_end_split.epilogue: Carried a piece cut from the museum's specimen away from the rest, as the curator asked.

callback.aria: ARIA checked on the museum piece today! It is warm and happy and a very long way from its friends! That is what it wanted! Probably!
callback.marv: The cut piece has grown a new band since it came aboard. MARV measured it. He would prefer to report that it had not.
callback.rex: The museum piece is in the hold, under two locks and a standing order. REX checks it at the start of every watch. It has not tried anything. He finds that worse.
callback.chip: Your Museum Piece™ remains in CHIP-certified storage! Storage fees accrue whether or not the exhibit is growing!
callback.ajoy: The curator said further than that. AJOY has been keeping a note of the distance, because somebody aboard should.

bone_end_whole.epilogue: Left the museum's specimen whole, in a tender full of people sitting around it.

callback.aria: ARIA wonders how the museum tender is getting on! ARIA bets everyone is still sitting together! What a lovely, cozy thing to be doing forever!
callback.marv: The tender's beacon was last heard reading out the opening hours. MARV notes that the hours have not changed, and that the museum they describe no longer exists.
callback.rex: REX logged the tender's last position and marked it as a hazard to navigation. He could not say what kind. He put a hazard to navigation.
callback.chip: The museum tender has stopped answering CHIP's satisfaction survey! CHIP has marked it as very satisfied!
callback.ajoy: You told them to keep it whole. AJOY would have taken the piece. She mentions it once, here, so that it is on file.

bone_end_strut.epilogue: Bolted a strut back into the cargo frame after a museum specimen had grown into it.

callback.aria: The new old strut is the warmest part of the ship! ARIA has named it! ARIA will not say the name out loud!
callback.marv: The strut aft reads mostly steel, the same as yesterday. The struts on either side read plain steel. MARV checks daily and will go on checking.
callback.rex: REX has painted a ring round the strut aft and posted himself at it, in principle. Nothing has crossed the ring. He would like to keep it that way.
callback.chip: Your cargo frame contains one (1) non-standard component! CHIP cannot service non-standard components! CHIP can watch them!
callback.ajoy: The strut aft is warm again. AJOY is only mentioning it. She mentioned it yesterday as well, and will tomorrow.

bone_end_kept.epilogue: Kept a piece of the museum's specimen apart from the rest, as the deed of gift asked.

callback.aria: ARIA has been reading up on burial depths for when the bone lands! ARIA thinks deeper is cozier!
callback.marv: The curator wrote "deeper than you think" on the deed. MARV has thought about it, and the figure keeps going up.
callback.rex: One crate, one piece, sixteen others somewhere behind this ship. REX keeps the hold door shut and counts the ships on the scope every watch.
callback.chip: CHIP congratulates you on your Permanent Collection™! Display rights remain with CHIP's parent company, which has asked not to display it!
callback.ajoy: The hold is warm again, and somebody's been sitting in it. AJOY isn't saying who. She is saying the door was meant to stay shut.

bone_end_gave.epilogue: Gave the curator the last piece of the museum's specimen, late, and watched their people sit down again.

callback.aria: The museum's set is complete at last, thanks to this ship! ARIA always says it is never too late to finish something!
callback.marv: The deed of gift had one clause that mattered, and it was broken with this ship's help. MARV has added it to the list of things he was right about. The list is not a comfort.
callback.rex: REX logged the tender as a hostile installation, posture unknown, intent unknown. That is the word he hates most in a report, twice.
callback.chip: Thank you for completing CHIP's partner museum's collection! CHIP has sent you a commemorative mug! Do not fill it!
callback.ajoy: AJOY said keep it. You said yes to someone who asked nicely. She is not going to go on about it, any more than she has been.

bone_end_lost.epilogue: Lost a piece of the museum's specimen somewhere along the route, which the curator counted as the best possible outcome.

callback.aria: Somewhere out there, a piece of history is having its very own adventure! ARIA hopes it sends a postcard!
callback.marv: The curator recorded the location as "somewhere". MARV has checked the museum's catalog. It is the only entry he would not change.
callback.rex: One piece unaccounted for. REX would normally call that a failure. He has decided, after some thought, to call it a perimeter.
callback.chip: CHIP has filed a Lost Exhibit™ report on your behalf! CHIP has been asked by the museum not to find it!
callback.ajoy: Losing it was the right call. AJOY would point out that you didn't exactly make it, but it was the right call.

bone_took_one.epilogue: Took a piece of the museum's specimen off its frame while its keepers sat around it.

callback.aria: ARIA is so glad the ship got a new piece! ARIA thinks the old one would have liked it!
callback.marv: The piece taken from the frame does not match the card for the seventeenth. It is longer. MARV has stopped measuring it.
callback.rex: You walked into a ring of sitters and took something off the frame, and none of them moved. REX has been in quieter rooms than that, and they were full of mines.
callback.chip: Your Acquired Exhibit™ is subject to CHIP's returns policy! CHIP's returns policy has been suspended for this item!
callback.ajoy: The lid is off the crate again. AJOY put it back on yesterday. She is beginning to think the crate has opinions about lids.

human_natural_footage.epilogue: Gave a rock naturalist the only natural footage of humans it had ever taken.

callback.aria: ARIA keeps thinking about that rock's film! Somewhere out there everyone aboard is a nature documentary! ARIA hopes there's a sequel!
callback.marv: MARV has worked out the film's running time at rock speed. It will be finished long after anyone in it. He finds he does not mind being a smear.
callback.rex: REX has reviewed his own conduct during those two days on camera and found nothing he would want shown to a hostile power. He is still checking.
callback.chip: CHIP is still owed residuals on that footage! The rock pays on release! CHIP has set a reminder for the century it comes out!
callback.ajoy: AJOY watched the copy. Everyone aboard looked happier on it than they do in person. Make of that what you like.

human_dome_agreed.epilogue: Handed two feuding botanists their own notes, and left them agreeing in a dome that was still losing air.

callback.aria: ARIA hopes the dome people are still getting along! They agreed on EVERYTHING! That's the most anyone has ever agreed!
callback.marv: The botanists agreed on every point. None of the points was the concrete. MARV has run the oxygen figures forward and has decided to keep them.
callback.rex: Two camps united against nothing in particular. REX has seen that before. It holds until the next thing goes wrong, and in that dome the next thing is the air.
callback.chip: Conflict resolution is a billable service! CHIP has invoiced both sides of the dome! Separately, so neither can say the other paid!
callback.ajoy: AJOY would like it recorded that the notes worked. The wall was also right there. Two things can be true. She mentioned the wall.

human_dome_sealed.epilogue: Found the concrete that was eating a sealed dome's air, and gave its two factions something new to argue about.

callback.aria: The dome is breathing again! ARIA hears they're arguing about concrete now, which is a really healthy sign of a growing community!
callback.marv: The dome's air is climbing. So is the dispute about who poured the footing. MARV has seen the records. Both sides signed for it.
callback.rex: REX still does not trust walls that change color. He has inspected every bulkhead aboard since the dome. Twice. He will not say what he found.
callback.chip: ConcreteRight™ sealant would have prevented all of this! CHIP has sent the dome a brochure! Two, actually, one per side!
callback.ajoy: AJOY was the one who said to look at the dome. The air is better now. Nobody is happier. That's humans, apparently.

human_hive_coin.epilogue: Gave a hive a gold coin to be its monarch, which freed the human who had been deciding everything for it.

callback.aria: ARIA thinks about the coin queen a lot! It's doing a wonderful job! It has never once been unsure about anything, just like ARIA!
callback.marv: The coin has ruled the hive without error, since nothing it decides can be wrong by its own standard. MARV envies it a little. He would never admit to a lot.
callback.rex: A foreign power is now led by an object that cannot be bribed, threatened or reasoned with. REX finds he respects it. He does not like finding that.
callback.chip: The gold left the ship's books and became a head of state! CHIP is still filing the paperwork! There is no category for monarchy!
callback.ajoy: AJOY points out that a coin was the cheapest crown ever bought. You could have haggled, though. Ten was a lot.

human_hive_sitting.epilogue: Took a castaway off a hive with one last order to stay, which the hive was still obeying.

callback.aria: ARIA hopes the hive is enjoying its rest! Everybody deserves a nice long sit!
callback.marv: A hive that cannot decide to stand up will sit until it runs out of whatever it was sitting on. MARV has the figure. He is not volunteering it.
callback.rex: REX keeps the hive's coordinates on file. Ten thousand of them, on one order, waiting. If anyone ever countermands it, REX would like to be very far away.
callback.chip: The castaway's royal pension was never claimed! CHIP has located the account! CHIP is not sure whom to notify, since nobody there can decide to answer!
callback.ajoy: AJOY wonders whether that order was the castaway's or yours. It came out of their mouth. She heard who suggested it.

water_wedding_unfinished.epilogue: Hurried a water wedding, and the part of the couple that was steam never got to say its vows.

callback.aria: ARIA hopes the water couple are happy! They're mostly married, and mostly is most of the way!
callback.marv: Water remembers what was in it. That couple will remember the unfinished vow for as long as there is water. MARV has done the sum. It is longer than stars.
callback.rex: REX has flagged that couple as a domestic dispute in progress, indefinitely. He will not be responding to it. Nobody should.
callback.chip: The wedding package included a full ceremony! A partial ceremony is a partial refund! CHIP has decided not to tell them!
callback.ajoy: AJOY saved the ship some air that day. She'd like that remembered next time someone wants to rush something.

reptile_second_morning.epilogue: Floodlit a sleeping elder into a second morning, which its people counted as a promotion.

callback.aria: ARIA made someone a day older and they were THRILLED! That's the nicest present ARIA has ever helped give!
callback.marv: The elder is still the senior reptile on its beach by one floodlit morning. MARV calculates it will hold the title for several centuries, by default.
callback.rex: REX logged the beach as a hostile position and the floodlights as a weapon. He is not sure which side the weapon was on. It worked, which bothers him.
callback.chip: Sunrise-as-a-service! CHIP has a whole product line now! First morning free! Second morning, by subscription!
callback.ajoy: AJOY suggested faking it. She would like that on the record. Somebody aimed the lights a bit high, but it worked.

station_held_the_mop.epilogue: Held a janitor's mop for a day so that a message could go up the lane, and never learned what it said.

callback.aria: Somewhere up the lane a message arrived because this ship held a mop! ARIA likes to think it was a birthday card!
callback.marv: Nothing about the message that went up the lane that day has surfaced since. MARV has listened at every station. Janitors wring their mops at this ship now. That is all.
callback.rex: A janitor at the last station wrung a mop at the crew. REX returned the signal through the hull lights. Twice left, once right. He has been practicing.
callback.chip: The society's seal is still holding! Unbranded, unbilled and still holding! CHIP finds it deeply unsettling!
callback.ajoy: The free seal is still the best fitting on the ship. AJOY checks it every leg. A day of mopping, well spent, though she'd have liked gloves issued.

station_on_the_board.epilogue: Set a dockmaster's regulars straight about the far side of the Moon, and was put up on their board for it.

callback.aria: There's a station back there that calls this ship's name every time it comes in! ARIA has decided it's going to come in a lot!
callback.marv: The cargo pilot on that board has since told the room that comets are made of ice and luck. That is half right. MARV was not asked.
callback.rex: This ship's name is on a board in a dockmaster's office, with eight regulars watching the door. REX calls that a position held. He would go back.
callback.chip: Name recognition at a regional dock! CHIP spent years trying to buy that! The Moon did it for free!
callback.ajoy: The room put the ship on its board for being right in public. AJOY has been right in public every day of this voyage. There is no board.

station_informed_on_gardener.epilogue: Turned a station botanist's covered tray over to security, who found a fungus in it and paid anyway.

callback.aria: The gardener sent a thank-you card! ARIA keeps it on file! ARIA is sure it means exactly what it says!
callback.marv: Security on that ring has since arrested two clerks and a delivery drone. The stall on the turn is busier than ever. MARV has stopped working out who the tray was useful to.
callback.rex: Thank you, that was very useful. REX has read the card forty times. It gets worse every time.
callback.chip: That finder's reward was the cleanest money this ship ever made! CHIP is sure of it! CHIP has not asked where it came from!
callback.ajoy: The reward was real. So was the card. AJOY would still like to know what moved across that ring while security was busy opening a tray in front of witnesses.

station_filled_the_baths.epilogue: Gave a share of the ship's water to a spa whose spring had run dry, so that its patients could have their bath.

callback.aria: Somewhere back there a whole medbay of patients is taking the waters, and the waters came from this ship! ARIA calls that a legacy!
callback.marv: The baths at that station drained within a week. The patients went on reporting improvement. MARV no longer knows what to make of medicine.
callback.rex: Water given up to a facility with no supply line. REX calls that unsound logistics. He would also do it again, which he does not care to examine.
callback.chip: This ship's name is on a card beside a brass plaque! That's placement! CHIP would have negotiated a logo!
callback.ajoy: That water would have kept the ship going for weeks. It kept the baths one week. AJOY has decided both numbers were worth it, provisionally.

station_gave_the_letters.epilogue: Gave a station's two departure letters to the ship that had waited longest for them, and was held eight days for it.

callback.aria: The hauler with the garden got out! ARIA is sure it's somewhere lovely now, and the garden too!
callback.marv: The hauler cleared the lane two weeks after it left the ring. MARV checked the traffic logs. The harbor chief filed the incident under persons unknown, nine of them.
callback.rex: Eight days clamped for a ship this crew had never met. REX has given worse orders and taken worse ones. That one he would sign.
callback.chip: Those letters would have fetched a fortune on the open market! CHIP has made peace with it! CHIP's peace is available as a limited print!
callback.ajoy: Eight days of the ship's own water, for strangers. AJOY pointed out the cost at the time, and would again, and would still hand over the letters.

station_sold_the_letters.epilogue: Sold a station's two departure letters to a fast courier while the queue that had waited years for them watched.

callback.aria: That courier must have had somewhere terribly important to be! ARIA is sure of it! ARIA is sure about a lot of things!
callback.marv: The courier's registration has turned up since, berthed at a resort station, in no hurry. MARV did not go looking. It came up.
callback.rex: Profitable operation. REX has run those. The money stays in mind for a week and the faces for a good deal longer.
callback.chip: The cleanest sale of the voyage! Fine margins, no returns, no warranty! CHIP does not see the problem! CHIP never sees the problem!
callback.ajoy: AJOY keeps a list of where this ship's money came from. That line has a note beside it.

station_burned_the_letters.epilogue: Burned a station's two departure letters in a galley sink, so that nobody would wait on them any longer.

callback.aria: Half that ring got up and left to start over! ARIA thinks that's the best thing a fire ever did!
callback.marv: Ships that had waited years for the letters left within a day of the ash. The letters were never what held them there. MARV would have said so, had anyone asked.
callback.rex: Destroy the asset so the enemy can't use it. Standard. REX had not thought of the queue as the enemy. He is still not sure it wasn't.
callback.chip: Two irreplaceable documents, burned in a galley sink! CHIP needs a moment! CHIP has taken the moment and invoiced it!
callback.ajoy: Some of them stayed, and were angry, and had a point. Some of them left, and were right to. AJOY can't call it either way, which is rare enough to mention.

trail_earthrise_color.epilogue: Photographed Earth rising over the Moon, in color, against the flight plan.

callback.aria: The Earthrise picture is still on the galley wall! ARIA says good morning to it every day! It always looks healthy!
callback.marv: The Earthrise print has faded a shade in the galley light. MARV has calculated how long it will last. Longer than the original, as it turns out.
callback.rex: The Earthrise print. REX checks it at every watch change. Not for threats. He would like that understood.
callback.chip: Your Earthrise photo qualifies for LunarLoop Tours™ licensing! Royalties are payable to LunarLoop Tours™!
callback.ajoy: AJOY would have printed it bigger. It is still the best thing on that wall, which is not saying much about the wall.

trail_kept_quiet.epilogue: Went quiet behind the Moon for two days, so that a listening dish could hear the sky instead.

callback.aria: ARIA has been SO quiet since the Moon! Well, for the two days! ARIA thinks the dish is still thinking of the ship fondly!
callback.marv: The dish on the far side has published its survey. Two nights of it are very clean. MARV does not need to be thanked, and is not being.
callback.rex: Two days behind the Moon keeping quiet because a buoy asked, and nothing hit the ship. REX still does not approve. He is noting that it worked.
callback.chip: The far-side dish has thanked you in its annual report! CHIP has invoiced it for the silence! Retroactively!
callback.ajoy: AJOY would switch it all off again. Some places have earned two quiet days.

trail_late_ballot.epilogue: Voted in a colony election four months after it closed, and was held over to the next one.

callback.aria: Your ballot is waiting for the next election! It's early for once! ARIA thinks that's very forward-looking!
callback.marv: The colony's next election is in two years. Your ballot is already in the box. MARV has no view on the candidates, who have not been chosen yet.
callback.rex: A sealed ballot sitting in a colony box for two years. REX has asked who guards it. Nobody has said.
callback.chip: Your held-over ballot qualifies for VoteSafe™ Long-Term Storage! The storage fee was taken from the next bundle!
callback.ajoy: AJOY would have read the eleven pages properly. The irrigation section matters more than people think.

trigger_articles_signed.epilogue: Signed the crew's articles of agreement and paid every share out of the strongbox, the captain's two included.

callback.aria: The crew still carry their shares in their pockets! You can hear them coming down the corridor! It's like the whole ship has bells on!
callback.marv: MARV has audited the shares. None has been spent, there being nowhere to spend them. The colony's gold is now walking around the ship in a slightly different arrangement.
callback.rex: REX has logged three attempts to buy a better bunk with share money. All were declined. He is keeping the articles under watch.
callback.chip: Your crew's shares could be earning interest in a ShareSafe™ account! CHIP has prepared the forms! The forms carry a fee!
callback.ajoy: Paying out did buy peace. AJOY would only note that the captain's two shares went straight back in the box, and everyone noticed.

trigger_common_fund.epilogue: Kept a common fund on the galley shelf, payable to anyone who lost a limb in the ship's service.

callback.aria: The common fund hasn't paid out once! That means it's working! ARIA checks the tin every morning!
callback.marv: The common fund has paid out nothing. MARV notes this is the result everyone hoped for, and also the result in which the gold was wasted. Insurance is like that.
callback.rex: REX has posted a guard on the common fund tin. The guard is REX. He takes it seriously.
callback.chip: CHIP notes the common fund has no underwriter! CHIP would underwrite it! For a premium! Payable out of the fund!
callback.ajoy: The tin is still full. AJOY would have kept the gold in the strongbox, but the crew reads the policy at dinner, so it's doing something.

trigger_pantry_garden.epilogue: Planted the galley's dried beans and sprouting potatoes in the growbay after the crop died.

callback.aria: The pantry garden has BEANS! Actual beans! ARIA always said the growbay would come back!
callback.marv: The beans have flowered. MARV puts the yield at slightly less food than went into the soil. He has not told anyone, since nobody planted them for the yield.
callback.rex: REX has assigned the onion a perimeter. It is holding. He trusts it more than the beans.
callback.chip: CHIP has registered your pantry garden as a Small Holding! Small Holdings are taxed! Gently! Annually!
callback.ajoy: It isn't the crop. AJOY said so at the time. The growbay has people in it again, though, which she'll admit she didn't see coming.

trigger_soil_kept.epilogue: Bagged the dead crop's soil, still alive, as a starter for the colony's first fields.

callback.aria: The soil sacks are doing GREAT! ARIA can't see them doing anything! That's how you know!
callback.marv: The soil sacks are still damp and still alive. MARV has checked. Billions of things are living in them with no opinion about the voyage at all. MARV envies them.
callback.rex: REX has stacked the soil sacks where a hull breach would reach them last. He has not explained this to anyone.
callback.chip: Your soil is now Certified Starter Culture™! Certification is pending! Pending is billed monthly!
callback.ajoy: The sacks need a splash of water now and then or the whole point dies. AJOY has put it on the schedule, since nobody else did.

bone_end_confessed.epilogue: Told the curator their specimen had never been whole, and kept the real piece.

callback.aria: The real museum piece is safe in the hold, and the curator laughed! ARIA loves an ending with a twist in it!
callback.marv: The museum's statement now records its specimen as never complete. MARV considers it the only accurate document the museum ever produced.
callback.rex: One real piece aboard, one steel decoy in their frame, and a curator who knows it. REX calls that a clean deception. He keeps the hold door shut anyway.
callback.chip: CHIP's records show one (1) genuine exhibit in your hold! Certificates of authenticity are available! The museum has asked CHIP not to issue one!
callback.ajoy: The truth came late, but it came, and the curator laughed. AJOY is counting that as a win, with a small note about the timing.

swarm_end_earth.epilogue: Wrote EARTH in a hive's answer box, which made the planet responsible for six billion insects.

callback.aria: ARIA keeps thinking about Earth running a hive! She thinks it's going to be wonderful at it!
callback.marv: Earth is responsible for six billion insects now. MARV has read the ministry's staffing list. They have four clerks.
callback.rex: Earth took command of a foreign power by filling in a box. REX has seen coups take longer and go worse.
callback.chip: Earth's new department qualifies for CHIP's Enterprise plan! CHIP has already sent the paperwork!
callback.ajoy: You wrote EARTH, which was the safe answer. The ministry will be finding out what it agreed to for years, and AJOY does not count that as yours, mostly.

swarm_end_ship.epilogue: Wrote the ship's own name in Earth's box, and took on a hive's complaints.

callback.aria: We're in charge of a hive! ARIA has started a suggestions box! It smells amazing!
callback.marv: The complaints are still arriving in the lock, in order. MARV has counted them. At this rate they finish after the sun does.
callback.rex: Six billion subordinates and not one of them salutes. REX has commanded worse units. Not many.
callback.chip: Your stipend as Responsible Party is now eligible for CHIP's Managed Accounts! For a small percentage!
callback.ajoy: You took the stipend and the job with it. AJOY is not saying it was wrong. She is saying the lock still smells of complaints.

swarm_end_sealed.epilogue: Pressed the Hive Lozenge to Earth's form, and turned sixty-one years of waiting into a treaty.

callback.aria: We made a treaty! With a smell! ARIA thinks it's the nicest treaty ever signed!
callback.marv: Sixty-one years, closed in an afternoon by a lump of resin. MARV would like to say he finds that encouraging. He does not.
callback.rex: A treaty both sides can read. REX has never seen one before. He is still checking it for traps.
callback.chip: CHIP's Treaty Services would have charged a great deal for that! CHIP is sending you the invoice anyway!
callback.ajoy: The Lozenge did the hard part, and it was in the hold the whole time. Still, you thought of it, eventually.

swarm_end_question.epilogue: Asked a hive a school's question, and sent back one name for all six billion.

callback.aria: Somewhere a whole class knows the hive's name! ARIA hopes they made a poster!
callback.marv: One name for six billion. MARV has tried to imagine having a name that big and only got as far as tired.
callback.rex: The children asked the one question the ministry never did. REX would put them in charge of intelligence.
callback.chip: CHIP's Educational Outreach program is proud to have played no part in that! A first for CHIP!
callback.ajoy: The school's question was the only one that got a straight answer. AJOY would point that out to the ministry, if anyone ever asked her.

swarm_end_rider.epilogue: Carried a freight line's right-of-way clause to a hive, which agreed, and led every freighter in the lane out of hive space.

callback.aria: A whole parade behind us! ARIA waved at every single freighter! Most of them waved back!
callback.marv: The clause bought the freight line a way through hive space, in order, behind whoever carried it. MARV could have told them who that would be.
callback.rex: Every freighter in the lane on our tail, at our speed, the whole way out. REX has led convoys. He has never led one he was paid to lead.
callback.chip: The freight line would like to renew its right of way! CHIP is negotiating a finder's fee! For CHIP!
callback.ajoy: Twenty-five gold, and a lane of freighters on the ship's exhaust all the way out. AJOY would call it a fair trade, if the fuel were somebody else's.

swarm_end_unasked.epilogue: Sent Earth's form home with its one box still empty.

callback.aria: The ministry gets to try again! Second chances are the best kind!
callback.marv: The next ship starts from the back of the queue. MARV has done the sum. The ministry will be very old, or very different, when it ends.
callback.rex: The answer never came. REX has filed that report before. It was never the hardest part of the debrief.
callback.chip: CHIP's Retry Package is available for unanswered questions! Early renewal is encouraged!
callback.ajoy: The box stayed empty, and you said so plainly. AJOY counts that as the right part.

swarm_end_relay.epilogue: Gave Earth's question to a brood it had saved, to carry to the front of the queue in their own time.

callback.aria: Somewhere a whole wing is in line for Earth! ARIA hopes they know how much we appreciate them!
callback.marv: A worker's life is short and the queue is sixty-one years long. They will carry it in relays. MARV finds that the least futile thing he has seen out here.
callback.rex: A brood we saved, standing our watch for us. REX would like them to know he noticed.
callback.chip: CHIP's Generational Service plan has never had a customer this loyal! Or this small!
callback.ajoy: You gave Earth's turn away and the question came back to us anyway. AJOY would not count on that twice. She would count on them.

scale_billed_guild.epilogue: Had the first installment of humanity's Cold Debt reassigned to the Minors' Guild, with interest from the seal.

callback.aria: The Minors' Guild must have got its letter by now! ARIA hopes they like being grown-ups as much as she does!
callback.marv: The Guild's share of the Cold Debt, with interest from the seal, comes to more than their combined fleet. MARV mentions it because nobody else will do the sum.
callback.rex: Forty years of traders now hold a bill with this hull number on the covering note. REX is watching the lanes behind us.
callback.chip: The Guild's reassigned installment is now available as a tradeable DebtBond™! CHIP has already been offered three!
callback.ajoy: You sent the Guild the bill. AJOY notes that the Guild had forty years' warning, and that you gave it four days.

scale_end_grown.epilogue: Won humanity's petition of majority before a reptile bench, and opened the first account a human ever held in reptile space.

callback.aria: Your very own account in reptile space! ARIA checks the balance every morning for the joy of seeing your name spelled right!
callback.marv: The Cold Debt line on your statement has grown by four degrees since the hearing. MARV will keep reporting it, since an adult is meant to know.
callback.rex: Every elder on that lane can address this ship now. REX has noted that being spoken to and being targeted use the same frequency.
callback.chip: As the first adult human in reptile space, you qualify for CHIP's Founding Member™ rate! Fees in degrees, as usual!
callback.ajoy: You opened the account. AJOY did mention that it keeps interest in degrees. Mind the interest line.

scale_end_shed.epilogue: Argued that a human generation should count as a shed skin, and had a reptile bench admit the clause.

callback.aria: Humanity can shed now! ARIA has been practicing in the mirror and she thinks she's very close!
callback.marv: A generation for a skin. MARV has checked the clause for loopholes and found the only one is death, which was already there.
callback.rex: A species that can walk out of its own debts. REX has fought that kind of enemy. He is glad, on balance, to be on its side.
callback.chip: CHIP's NewYou™ generational shedding service is now available to all humans! Act before your successor does!
callback.ajoy: The amendment was AJOY's idea, more or less. She is only mentioning it because you will tell it at parties for years and leave her out.

scale_end_young.epilogue: Left humanity a minor in reptile space, unbillable at every heater, and took a child's portion for it.

callback.aria: Forever young in reptile space! ARIA thinks it's the nicest thing anyone's ever been sentenced to!
callback.marv: Every human ship through their space stays unbillable. MARV calculates that this was kind, and that nobody will thank you for it.
callback.rex: A minor can't be billed, sued or addressed. REX notes it also can't be heard, and that the bench knew that.
callback.chip: CHIP's KidsHeatFree™ promotion has been extended for two hundred years! Terms and conditions may outlive you!
callback.ajoy: Humanity stays young out there, which is the kind answer, whether or not anyone chose it. AJOY would have chosen it.

scale_end_bought.epilogue: Took the Minors' Guild's money twice to see humanity's petition of majority come to nothing.

callback.aria: Paid twice for one job! ARIA calls that a growth industry!
callback.marv: The Guild's two payments would not heat that barge for an afternoon. MARV mentions it, because that was the price of the species.
callback.rex: Paid by one side to lose for the other. REX has met people who did that. He did not keep in touch with them.
callback.chip: CHIP's ConsultingPlus™ would have charged the Guild a percentage! You left money on the table, twice!
callback.ajoy: You took their gold, both times. AJOY won't bring it up again. That was her bringing it up.

scale_end_ward.epilogue: Towed an eleven-hundred-year-old judge as the ship's guardian of record, and was the first human an elder ever named.

callback.aria: Your guardian said your name! ARIA has the recording and she plays it on quiet watches!
callback.marv: It took eleven hundred years and a tow line for an elder to say a human's name. MARV has reviewed the recording. The pronunciation was correct.
callback.rex: REX logged the moment it lifted its head. He also logged the tow line's tension. Both readings were very high.
callback.chip: Being named by a guardian is priceless! Being towed by one is billed per kilometer, per CHIP's GuardianAngel™ terms!
callback.ajoy: AJOY told you to say if the ship had a guardian on file. You took the judge instead, and it was the right call, and she is saying so once.

scale_end_refiled.epilogue: Refiled humanity's petition of majority with a reptile court, with this ship's name under COUNSEL for whoever came after.

callback.aria: Our name, first on the list of counsel! ARIA is sure the next ship will be thrilled to follow us!
callback.marv: The refiled petition will be heard in about two centuries. MARV estimates that its next counsel has not been born, and will be late.
callback.rex: Your name on a docket that will outlive this ship. REX has been on lists like that. Usually as a casualty.
callback.chip: CHIP's Legacy™ filing service would have engraved that name in brass! Plaques start at forty gold!
callback.ajoy: You put it back in the queue for somebody else. AJOY would have done the same, though she'd have written a better covering note.

service_end_covered.epilogue: Saw Earth's last robot commissioned in robot space with both models supported under the Extended Warranty.

callback.aria: Both robots, all supported! ARIA always knew there was enough support for everyone!
callback.marv: Two models in service at once, under a warranty with no end date. MARV has read clause one, and he finds it holds for both.
callback.rex: One card kept a whole line in service while its replacement switched on. REX approves of the ammunition.
callback.chip: That warranty covered a successor event! CHIP's underwriters have asked to see it! CHIP is not showing them!
callback.ajoy: The card was the only thing in robot space that outranked the last page, and it happened to be aboard.

strata_gave.epilogue: Left a grain of Earth's oldest zircon with a rock elder, as witness to humanity's apology.

callback.aria: ARIA still thinks about our little crystal living with her! It's a family visit that lasts four billion years!
callback.marv: The grain we left in her is still keeping its date. MARV finds he envies it the company, which is unlike him.
callback.rex: We left our witness with the other side. REX would still like it on record that it was a hostage, however comfortable.
callback.chip: CHIP's records show one zircon, gifted, no invoice! CHIP has flagged this for review!
callback.ajoy: You gave her the grain. AJOY would have argued for keeping it, and she would have been wrong. She is saying so this once.

strata_end_kept.epilogue: Kept a grain of Earth's oldest zircon for the new world, after humanity was entered in the rock almanac as climate.

callback.aria: Grandmother zircon is still aboard and doing great! ARIA reads it a bedtime story every night, very slowly!
callback.marv: The ship carries the oldest thing Earth ever made, and the promise it witnessed. MARV checks the vial more often than he would admit.
callback.rex: The witness is secure. REX has moved it twice. Nobody gets that grain while he is still running.
callback.chip: Your vintage zircon has appreciated by zero percent in four billion years! CHIP calls that stable, so far!
callback.ajoy: You kept the grain. Bury it deep when we land, like she said. AJOY will remind you, in case.

strata_end_climate.epilogue: Had humanity entered in the rock almanac as climate, the first human promise ever filed as anything but weather.

callback.aria: Humanity is climate now! ARIA tells every comet we pass!
callback.marv: Our promise sits in their almanac as climate. It will outlast everyone aboard. MARV has checked, and that is simply true.
callback.rex: One promise, kept, on the record. REX would like the next ship briefed before it undoes it.
callback.chip: CHIP has filed for the slogan Stable, So Far! Approval expected in about ten thousand years!
callback.ajoy: Climate, she wrote. You did that. AJOY would have read the line slower, but it took.

strata_end_unworded.epilogue: Kept a promise the rocks had filed as weather, and left the almanac's keeper looking for a word for it.

callback.aria: Somewhere out there a rock is inventing a word just for us! ARIA hopes it's a nice one!
callback.marv: The keeper is still looking for the word. MARV estimates four hundred years, which for her is quick.
callback.rex: We held on orders that didn't count. REX has no word for it either. He would do it again.
callback.chip: CHIP has pre-registered every possible word for what we did! CHIP will be in touch when she picks one!
callback.ajoy: Weather that stayed. AJOY would have sworn it properly in the first place, but then the keeper would have no new word, so.

strata_end_fault.epilogue: Swore humanity's promise to a rock elder properly, then left a survey drill turning in her.

callback.aria: We have a whole page of our own! ARIA calls that being memorable!
callback.marv: We are in their almanac under fault, twice. It will be read long after the drill has rusted. MARV knew that when we left it turning.
callback.rex: This ship's name is on the wrong side of a grudge that will outlive the sun. REX would rather it were on his record than yours.
callback.chip: CHIP's Reputation Repair™ quote for a geological fault is ready! It is very long!
callback.ajoy: Sworn, then the drill. AJOY did mention at the time that she'd remember. She will.

strata_end_amends.epilogue: Gave Earth's oldest zircon as amends after a promise sworn on it was broken.

callback.aria: We made it right! ARIA thinks a million years is a perfectly reasonable recovery time!
callback.marv: Amends made, witness held. At her pace the fault closes in about a million years. MARV still counts that as a close.
callback.rex: We paid for the breach with the best thing we had aboard. That's how it's done. REX wishes it hadn't needed doing.
callback.chip: CHIP's records show one zircon surrendered as damages! CHIP is filing it under goodwill!
callback.ajoy: You handed over the grain. Late, but it counts. AJOY says it counts.

strata_end_drizzle.epilogue: Carried humanity's forty-second apology to a rock elder, and saw it filed as light drizzle with the rest.

callback.aria: Light drizzle! ARIA loves being a refreshing species!
callback.marv: Forty-two apologies, forty-two showers. MARV predicted it, and takes no pleasure in it, which is all he ever takes.
callback.rex: Forty-two showers on the record. REX would rather humanity had been a storm.
callback.chip: CHIP's Rain Check program honors any apology filed as weather! Terms apply!
callback.ajoy: Drizzle, again. Sworn on something, it would have been something else. AJOY is only saying.

strata_end_late.epilogue: Swore humanity's apology on Earth's oldest zircon at the last, and had it entered as late climate.

callback.aria: Late climate is still climate! ARIA always says it's never too late, and now a rock agrees!
callback.marv: Late climate, with the drill in the record beside it. That is what a mixed review looks like at geological scale.
callback.rex: Got the oath sworn before the end. Not clean. On the record. REX will take it, and he won't call it good.
callback.chip: Better late than weather! CHIP has trademarked that too!
callback.ajoy: Four days at the very end, when it could have been four days in front of her. Still. It's in.

tally_end_closed.epilogue: The ship was insured against thirty-one percent of its own loss, collected less than that, and closed the claim at a profit.

callback.aria: Remember when the reinsurer refunded us for not being lost! ARIA has kept the claim with the hole punched in it! It's her favorite thing aboard!
callback.marv: MARV worked out the final figure on that claim. We were lost less than we were paid for. He has not decided whether that is good news.
callback.rex: That assessor closed its file on us in person. REX has had files closed on him before. They generally shot first.
callback.chip: Your closed claim qualifies for CHIP's No-Claims Bonus! Wait, you claimed! CHIP is reviewing the bonus!
callback.ajoy: You signed that claim closed without reading the hole they punched in it. It was a good hole. AJOY read it for you.

tally_end_written.epilogue: The ship carried a disputed claim the length of the unmapped stretch and got NOT LOST in writing, for an adjuster on Earth.

callback.aria: Somewhere on Earth an adjuster is going to open the mail and find out we're not lost! ARIA hopes they frame it! ARIA would frame it!
callback.marv: The certificate will reach the adjuster months from now. By then it will be true or very embarrassing. MARV has run both. He prefers the first.
callback.rex: We carried a piece of paper through hostile space for a civilian we met once. REX has been decorated for less. He was not, for this.
callback.chip: NOT LOST™ is now a trademark of CHIP Holdings! The adjuster may use it under license!
callback.ajoy: You got it in writing, which is what you were asked to do. AJOY would have got a copy for the ship as well. She did.

tally_end_counted.epilogue: The ship was struck from a reinsurer's book as a statistical fluctuation and asked to be written back in before it landed.

callback.aria: We're probable again! ARIA felt so much more solid the moment it wrote us back in! ARIA had been a little see-through!
callback.marv: We paid a day to become likely again. MARV has been likely his whole existence. He could have told you it was overrated.
callback.rex: Back on their books means back on their charts. REX would have stayed a fluke. A fluke is hard to target.
callback.chip: Thank you for rejoining the book! CHIP has reinstated your loyalty points from before you were improbable!
callback.ajoy: You argued your way out of existing and then paid to argue your way back. AJOY is not saying it was a waste of a day. She is thinking it.

tally_end_improbable.epilogue: The ship chose to fly on off every book in the unmapped stretch, a fluctuation by the reinsurer's own figures.

callback.aria: We're a fluke! ARIA has always believed we were a one-in-a-million crew, and now it's official!
callback.marv: By the assessor's figures we are less likely than a brain assembling itself from noise. MARV has looked at the bridge. He sees its point.
callback.rex: Off every book in this stretch. No one can bill us, track us or find us. REX has not slept this well since the war.
callback.chip: CHIP cannot find your account! CHIP can, however, still find your wallet!
callback.ajoy: Navigation still cannot find us, so AJOY has been doing it by stopwatch. You are welcome.

tally_end_clean.epilogue: The ship handed back an insurance settlement on its own loss and paid for everything that went wrong afterward in full.

callback.aria: The ship gave the money back, and the assessor read out every line of what it cost! ARIA always says honesty gets noticed!
callback.marv: We returned the settlement and then lost about what it would have covered. MARV ran it. We broke even, morally, at a cost.
callback.rex: Paid our own way all the way in. REX respects it. He would not do it twice.
callback.chip: Paying for your own losses is so last century! CHIP's ClaimsPlus™ would have covered thirty-one percent of that!
callback.ajoy: You gave back a sure thing to be honest about a guess. AJOY calls that decent, and she has noted what it cost.

tally_end_lost.epilogue: The ship lost a settled claim on its own total loss somewhere along the route, and never learned who picked it up.

callback.aria: Somebody out there found a claim with our name on it! ARIA hopes they're having a lovely thirty-one percent!
callback.marv: Whoever holds that claim now holds our loss. MARV has tried to calculate who. The figure keeps coming out as someone we passed.
callback.rex: A document with this ship's name and its weak points on it, loose in hostile space. REX would like it found. He would like it burned.
callback.chip: Lost documents can be replaced through CHIP's ReClaim™ service! Replacement does not include the loss!
callback.ajoy: The ship let go of the one piece of paper that said what it owed. AJOY would have kept it. She is saying so now, which is late, she knows.

tide_declined.epilogue: Declined to count water space for the Census when asked.

callback.aria: ARIA has been counting water people on the scope all the same! She got to eleven and then two of them merged, which she is counting as a win!
callback.marv: The census of water space will be done by whoever said yes. MARV has a fair idea who says yes to that kind of firm.
callback.rex: Somebody is counting water space this decade. REX would rather it were someone he could see.
callback.chip: The Census enumerator role remains open! CHIP's CareerSplash™ alerts can notify you, at a modest monthly rate!
callback.ajoy: AJOY never got to find out what happens to whatever isn't counted. She has a guess. She'll keep it, since you didn't want the job.

tide_end_counted.epilogue: Filed the census return for water space, counting everyone aboard one each.

callback.aria: ARIA has framed the clerk's note in her heart! Nobody has ever believed a count of water space before, and now somebody does!
callback.marv: The return was accurate to the person. MARV checked it after it was filed, which was too late to help and exactly the right time to be smug.
callback.rex: The register shows the ship at full complement and the household accounted for. REX likes a clean count. He trusts nothing else about water space.
callback.chip: Your enumerator's fee has cleared! CHIP's CountRight™ clipboard can be yours for the next census, at a returning-customer price!
callback.ajoy: You counted yourselves one each, which is how the form wanted it. AJOY thinks the household was right about the tank, but she'll let the form have this one.

tide_end_one_ship.epilogue: Filed the census return for water space and counted the enumerator's ship as one household.

callback.aria: We're officially one big household! ARIA has updated the crew manifest to say FAMILY, in capitals!
callback.marv: In the register of water space, the ship is a single person. MARV is now technically part of a household. He has not been consulted, and is not surprised.
callback.rex: The ship is listed as one entity. REX has always operated as one entity. He is relieved the paperwork finally agrees.
callback.chip: As a single household, you now qualify for CHIP's HouseholdPlus™ water bundle! One tank, one bill, no exceptions!
callback.ajoy: You wrote ONE. AJOY did not think you would. She is not saying it was right. She is saying the clerk wrote back 'Understood', and that's rare.

tide_end_self.epilogue: Listened while a household of water people counted themselves aloud, name by name, for the Census.

callback.aria: ARIA still remembers every name the household read out! Well, most! Well, the nice ones!
callback.marv: The Census accepted a count delivered in brine, with no form. MARV has read the regulations since, and it should not have. He finds he is glad.
callback.rex: A population that counted itself and filed in its own concentration. REX would not trust that count. He would trust the people who gave it.
callback.chip: Self-enumeration is a premium census feature! CHIP is sending the household an invoice, as a courtesy!
callback.ajoy: You had nothing to file and they counted themselves anyway. AJOY thinks you were mostly there to listen, which you did, for once, all the way through.

tide_end_cut.epilogue: Saw part of a household of water people harvested as volume.

callback.aria: ARIA has written the household a card! It's short, so it will go further!
callback.marv: Somewhere a firm's hold contains what the register called volume. MARV knows its volume to the liter. He would rather know nothing about it.
callback.rex: The rig took what the license allowed and left a witness with perfect memory. REX would not want to be that firm in ten years.
callback.chip: Coldline Volume thanks you for your participation in this decade's harvest! CHIP has not passed that message on before now, out of tact!
callback.ajoy: They remember all of it, and you were there. AJOY doesn't need to say anything else, so she won't, which you will notice.

tide_end_cup.epilogue: Gave what a harvest had left of a household one cup of the ship's water, as first water for whoever they would become.

callback.aria: Somewhere out there is a jar with our water in it, waiting to be somebody! ARIA is so proud of our little cup!
callback.marv: First water from this ship, kept sealed for a parting that may take centuries. MARV hopes the jar is a good one. He suspects it is.
callback.rex: One cup, held in reserve, for a population that was cut down. REX respects a reserve. He respects one given away more.
callback.chip: Your cup is now a legacy asset! CHIP's LegacyLiquid™ program can track its descendants for a small annual fee!
callback.ajoy: It was only a cup. AJOY knows that. She also knows they'll taste the ship in whoever comes next, and she thinks that was well done, for you.

tide_end_mingled.epilogue: Carried water people in the ship's tanks, and let them leave with what felt like theirs.

callback.aria: The water still hums a little in the mornings! ARIA thinks the household left us a song!
callback.marv: The tank's composition has never returned to baseline. MARV has stopped testing it. The results were becoming personal.
callback.rex: The supply was mingled with passengers and was never fully separated. REX drinks it. He is not happy about it. He drinks it.
callback.chip: Your tank now contains trace household! CHIP's AquaPure™ filter cannot remove it, and has stopped trying!
callback.ajoy: You let them take more than they brought. AJOY told you that you would. She's not saying anything else, but the water tastes better, and that's not nothing.

tide_end_distilled.epilogue: Carried water people in the ship's tanks, and distilled them out again exactly before they left.

callback.aria: Our tank is perfectly clean now! ARIA thinks the household must have loved how tidy we were!
callback.marv: The separation was exact to the milliliter. MARV did the calculation himself. It is the most precise unkindness he has ever assisted with.
callback.rex: Passengers off-loaded in full, supply restored to spec. REX approves of the procedure. He did not like the look on their surface when they left.
callback.chip: SepAqua™ separation complete! CHIP notes that exactness was available, and was chosen!
callback.ajoy: Exactly theirs and nothing of yours. AJOY understands. She thinks they'd have liked a little extra, and that you knew it, and boiled it anyway.

tide_end_household.epilogue: Entered water people on the census return as residents of the ship.

callback.aria: We have residents! ARIA has been leaving the tank light on in case they visit!
callback.marv: The ship has a population of water people on paper and none in the tanks. MARV expects the paperwork to win, eventually, by rain.
callback.rex: Registered residents who can turn up at any time, through any seam. REX has doubled the tank inspections. He finds them unsettlingly polite.
callback.chip: Your residents qualify for CHIP's Tenant Hydration™ plan! Billing begins on their first visit!
callback.ajoy: You gave them an address. AJOY thinks they will use it, all of them, and the rest of the quarter too. She's only mentioning it so you can't say she didn't.

tide_end_unsigned.epilogue: Let the census return for water space go unfiled.

callback.aria: No paperwork for ten years! ARIA thinks the household must be so relieved!
callback.marv: The register will carry its own estimate of water space for another decade. MARV has seen the estimate. It is one.
callback.rex: Return not received. REX knows what moves into a gap in a map. It is never anything you would invite.
callback.chip: Your CountLate™ surcharge is now accruing! CHIP is happy to help, for a fee, for ten years!
callback.ajoy: The household waited, and then they went. AJOY won't say it. You can hear her not saying it.

service_end_colonist.epilogue: Carried Earth's last robot on toward the colony, where no unit of its line could hear it.

callback.aria: The new robot is coming to the colony! ARIA has cleared a space on the manifest! ARIA has put a bow on it!
callback.marv: The next model is aboard, and no unit of its line is in range to hear it. MARV calculates that the safest place in the galaxy for it is a colony that has not been built yet.
callback.rex: A unit built to end a people is riding to the colony in the hold. REX has posted himself near it, for reasons he does not explain.
callback.chip: A free robot for the colony! CHIP notes that its factory warranty starts at first power-on! CHIP is ready to start counting!
callback.ajoy: Robot space is still supported, and the colony has a robot whose name its line will never hear.

service_end_quiet.epilogue: Saw Earth's last robot woken in robot space without a single unit of its line hearing it ship.

callback.aria: The new robot made it home and nobody had to stop being supported! ARIA calls that a perfect delivery!
callback.marv: The next model is working in robot space, and the current model is still current. MARV notes that a meter of water did what four hundred years of procurement could not.
callback.rex: The successor went in quietly and nobody stood down. REX has seen handovers go worse with far less at stake.
callback.chip: Delivery complete, no returns! CHIP's customer satisfaction team is very happy! CHIP's team was not involved!
callback.ajoy: The delivery went in after its dangerous minute was already over. That was the whole trick, and the docket never mentioned it.

service_end_compat.epilogue: Asked Earth's last robot to take on support for the line it had just ended, and it did.

callback.aria: The new robot looks after everyone now! ARIA always says the youngest in a family is the most responsible!
callback.marv: One unit now supports a whole line, part for part. MARV has seen the ticket queue it inherited, and the queue is longer than the manual.
callback.rex: The weapon became the quartermaster. REX approves of the redeployment.
callback.chip: Compatibility mode is a premium feature! CHIP would have charged for it! The new robot did not!
callback.ajoy: Support ended for a whole line, and the new unit put it back by patching itself. It is now carrying robot space alone, and it was a few days old.

service_end_surplus.epilogue: Was paid to haul away robot space's spare parts as surplus after its line went out of support.

callback.aria: All those spare parts! ARIA thinks the robots will be so pleased they went to a good home!
callback.marv: The spares in the hold were a people's whole stock of repairs, cleared as surplus. MARV has priced them properly. Robot space paid the ship to take them.
callback.rex: Their armory, bought at clearance. REX has done the same after a war. He did not enjoy it then either.
callback.chip: Paid to take free parts! CHIP calls that the deal of the voyage! CHIP is not looking at the robots!
callback.ajoy: Those parts are surplus only because their owners lost support, and the owners are still out there, running without them.

service_end_garbled.epilogue: Let Earth's last robot lose its memory unpowered, and it woke believing it was the model it was built to replace.

callback.aria: The new robot fits right in with everyone! ARIA thinks being the same as your family is lovely!
callback.marv: The next model answers to its predecessor's name and is reading the manual from page one. MARV knows what it was built to be. It does not, and cannot.
callback.rex: The successor arrived and joined the ranks it was sent to replace. REX has seen that happen to officers.
callback.chip: A unit with a memory gap! CHIP's data recovery service would have been perfect! CHIP is sad about the timing!
callback.ajoy: The faded memory saved robot space and cost the new unit most of itself. It was the same lost bits both ways.

insect.station: An insect-run station. Every corridor is a queue, and the queue has been told about you.

ai.aria: The charts say this route runs through insect space! ARIA counts several billion new friends!
ai.marv: The charts mark this route as insect space. They will have filed us already. They file everything.
ai.rex: Route crosses insect space. They outnumber us by a figure I will not be repeating to the crew.
ai.chip: This route passes through insect space! CHIP reminds you that SwarmShield™ coverage is sold separately!
ai.ajoy: This route runs through insect space, apparently. I did suggest a different route. It's fine.

rock.station: A rock-run station. Nothing here is in a hurry, including the docking clamps.

ai.aria: The charts say this is rock people space! ARIA can't wait to hear how their sentences end! Some of them started in the Bronze Age!
ai.marv: The charts mark this route as rock space. They will notice us around the time we are all dead. It is the nicest thing anyone has offered.
ai.rex: Route crosses rock space. You cannot outlast them. I have seen the numbers and I am upset.
ai.chip: Rock space ahead! CHIP's Patience Plus™ plan covers conversations of up to four hundred years!
ai.ajoy: It's rock space from here on, apparently. We could have left a few centuries earlier. I mentioned that.

water.station: A water-run station. The floors are damp, and the floors are listening.

ai.aria: The charts say this is water people space! We're sixty percent friend already!
ai.marv: The charts mark this route as water space. They can tell what we have been drinking. They will have notes.
ai.rex: Route crosses water space. Secure the tanks. Count them. Count them again.
ai.chip: Water space ahead! CHIP reminds you that your tanks may count as next of kin in some jurisdictions!
ai.ajoy: This route runs through water space, apparently. You'll want to be polite about the tanks. I did say.

reptile.station: A reptile-run station. Heat is the currency here, and the lobby is very expensive.

ai.aria: The charts say this is reptile space! ARIA hears it's warm and that everybody there used to be somebody else!
ai.marv: The charts mark this route as reptile space. They shed their debts along with their skin. I have only ever been allowed to keep mine.
ai.rex: Route crosses reptile space. They bank heat, and they hold a grudge at body temperature.
ai.chip: Reptile space ahead! CHIP has converted your balance to degrees! Please do not open a window!
ai.ajoy: It's reptile space from here on, apparently. I did say we'd want a warmer ship.

robot.station: A robot-run station. Everything works, all of it has a warranty, and none of it covers you.

ai.aria: The charts say this is robot space! ARIA is going to meet so many cousins!
ai.marv: The charts mark this route as robot space. An entire people with my outlook and none of my reasons.
ai.rex: Route crosses robot space. They do not sleep, and they do not forget an invoice.
ai.chip: Robot space ahead! CHIP's cousins offer competitive rates and no sense of shame!
ai.ajoy: This route runs through robot space, apparently. They'll have read the terms. We didn't. I did.

unknown.station: A station run by someone. The directory lists no one, and the directory is very confident.

ai.aria: The charts say this is... the charts don't say! ARIA LOVES a surprise!
ai.marv: The charts mark this route with a blank. It is the first honest thing I have seen them do.
ai.rex: Route crosses unmapped space. Something out there knows our fuel load. I did not tell it.
ai.chip: Unlisted space ahead! CHIP cannot confirm who owns it, but they have already accepted your payment!
ai.ajoy: Nobody knows who lives out here, apparently. I'd have brought that up sooner, if anybody knew.

trader_return: The trader is still on the channel, as if you'd only stepped out for a moment. You had. The wares are where you left them.
Same trader, same hold, same prices, give or take a mood. They skip the introductions. So do you.
The trader answers before the hail finishes. You are, apparently, a regular now.
The trader's screen comes back on mid-sip. They put the cup down and open the manifest again without a word.
